paras.en: With the tech market in turmoil due to rising interest rates, raging anti-AI sentiment and Nvidia's C-suite crisis, Anthropic's IPO was part exuberance, part relief for an industry hungry for exits.
paras.zh: 由于利率上升、反人工智能情绪高涨以及英伟达高管危机，科技市场陷入动荡，Anthropic 的 IPO 部分是繁荣，部分是对渴望退出的行业的缓解。

paras.en: After venture-backed IPOs yielded $73 billion in proceeds in 2021, the amount raised in the next four years totaled just $39 billion, according to data from University of Florida emeritus professor Jay Ritter. In 2021, 126 technology companies went public, compared with 34 in 2025.
paras.zh: 佛罗里达大学名誉教授杰伊·里特 (Jay Ritter) 的数据显示，在 2021 年风险投资支持的 IPO 产生了 730 亿美元收益后，未来四年筹集的资金总额仅为 390 亿美元。 2021 年，有 126 家科技公司上市，而 2025 年为 34 家。

paras.en: Meanwhile, the private market has continued to balloon, with companies raising ever-larger sums at sky-high valuations without the pressures of quarterly earnings. Many startups that had hoped to go public early in the decade fell out of favor in the AI boom. They experienced hefty job cuts, down rounds and acquisitions for pennies on the dollar.
paras.zh: 与此同时，私募市场继续膨胀，公司在没有季度盈利压力的情况下以极高的估值筹集了越来越多的资金。许多原本希望在本世纪初上市的初创公司在人工智能热潮中失宠。他们经历了大幅裁员、折价融资和低价收购。

paras.en: "There was a time in Silicon Valley not that long ago where the prevailing wisdom was the default path should be avoiding going public for as long as possible," said Somesh Dash, a general partner at venture firm IVP. The view was, "it's too long, it's too hard, it's not worth it," he said.
paras.zh: 风险投资公司 IVP 的普通合伙人萨梅什·达什 (Somesh Dash) 表示：“不久前，硅谷流行的观点是，默认路径应该是尽可能长时间地避免上市。”他说，人们的观点是，“太长、太难、不值得”。

paras.en: Anthropic is very young compared to some of those companies, but it was a huge collector of private capital. Investors poured $141 billion into the AI lab as of September, according to Anthropic's prospectus.
paras.zh: 与其中一些公司相比，Anthropic 还很年轻，但它是私人资本的巨大聚集者。根据 Anthropic 的招股说明书，截至 9 月份，投资者已向该人工智能实验室注资 1410 亿美元。

paras.en: For a few Silicon Valley firms that contributed to those funding rounds, the returns are unlike anything they've ever seen. At the IPO price, Menlo Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners each owned about $25 billion worth of Anthropic stock. Bessemer Venture Partners owned a stake worth roughly $10 billion, partner Byron Deeter said.
paras.zh: 对于一些参与这些融资轮次的硅谷公司来说，回报是他们从未见过的。按 IPO 价格计算，Menlo Ventures 和 Lightspeed Venture Partners 各自拥有价值约 250 亿美元的 Anthropic 股票。合伙人 Byron Deeter 表示，Bessemer Venture Partners 持有价值约 100 亿美元的股份。

paras.en: Matt Murphy, a partner at Menlo, told CNBC's David Faber on Thursday that his firm has more than five limited partners "that we delivered over $1 billion of returns to."
paras.zh: Menlo 合伙人马特·墨菲 (Matt Murphy) 周四对 CNBC 的 David Faber 表示，他的公司拥有超过 5 个有限合伙人，“我们为他们提供了超过 10 亿美元的回报”。

paras.en: "At the end of the day, that's really our job, is to get dollars back into foundations and endowments," Murphy said. "There's a lot of pride in being able to do that."
paras.zh: “归根结底，这确实是我们的工作，就是将资金重新投入基金会和捐赠基金，”墨菲说。 “能够做到这一点，我们感到非常自豪。”

paras.en: Bessemer's Deeter was also jubilant on Thursday, posting on X that, in addition to being "the largest bet in Bessemer's history," the IPO "is a punctuation mark in the history of both humanity and computation."
paras.zh: 周四，贝塞默的 Deeter 也很高兴，他在 X 上发帖称，此次 IPO 除了是“贝塞默历史上最大的赌注”之外，“还是人类历史和计算历史上的一个标点符号”。

paras.en: That's quite a change from a few years earlier, when Anthropic was hardly generating revenue, and success was far from guaranteed. In 2023, Anthropic's Claude 2 was struggling to keep pace with models from Google and OpenAI. In April 2024, investors at Bessemer wrote in a memo that if Anthropic missed its own targets, there was "a good chance that we lose all or part of our money."
paras.zh: 与几年前相比，这是一个很大的变化，当时 Anthropic 几乎无法产生收入，而且成功也远未得到保证。 2023 年，Anthropic 的 Claude 2 正在努力跟上 Google 和 OpenAI 模型的步伐。 2024 年 4 月，Bessemer 的投资者在一份备忘录中写道，如果 Anthropic 未能实现自己的目标，“我们很可能会损失全部或部分资金”。

paras.en: Guru Chahal at Lightspeed told CNBC that Anthropic was clearly the team taking a more measured approach to AI. The company looked beyond Nvidia's dominant AI chips, choosing to use alternatives from Amazon and Google as well. Anthropic said it generated $1.72 in revenue per dollar spent on computing power in the third quarter, up from 68 cents a year earlier.
paras.zh: Lightspeed 的 Guru Chahal 告诉 CNBC，Anthropic 显然是对人工智能采取更加谨慎的方法的团队。该公司不仅仅关注英伟达占主导地位的人工智能芯片，还选择使用亚马逊和谷歌的替代品。 Anthropic 表示，第三季度在计算能力上每花费 1 美元，就能带来 1.72 美元的收入，高于去年同期的 68 美分。

paras.en: "It is true that it required lots of capital, but when you dig in and you realize that capital is going toward compute, and this is the team that's positioned to use that compute in the most effective way, then we could connect those dots," Chahal said. He added that those metrics showed it was "going to be a very high-quality business."
paras.zh: 查哈尔说：“确实，这需要大量资本，但当你深入研究时，你会意识到资本正在流向计算，而这个团队能够以最有效的方式使用计算，那么我们就可以将这些点联系起来。”他补充说，这些指标表明它“将成为一家非常高质量的企业”。

paras.en: Anthropic isn't the only big win for VCs this year.
paras.zh: Anthropic 并不是今年风险投资公司唯一的重大胜利。

paras.en: Five months before Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, SpaceX hit the market in what, until this week, was by far the largest IPO in history. SpaceX, which Elon Musk founded in 2002, produced outsized returns for firms including Sequoia and Andreessen Horowitz.
paras.zh: 在 Anthropic 在纳斯达克首次亮相的五个月前，SpaceX 上市，直到本周，这还是迄今为止历史上规模最大的 IPO。埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 于 2002 年创立的 SpaceX 为红杉资本 (Sequoia) 和安德森·霍洛维茨 (Andreessen Horowitz) 等公司带来了巨额回报。

paras.en: SpaceX and Anthropic alone will make 2026 a monster year for the venture industry, easily exceeding any other year in IPO proceeds. And investors in OpenAI hope appetite remains strong for trillion-dollar companies next year, as the ChatGPT maker is looking to 2027 for a potential offering.
paras.zh: 仅 SpaceX 和 Anthropic 就将使 2026 年成为风险投资行业的怪兽年，其 IPO 收益轻松超过任何其他年份。 OpenAI 的投资者希望明年对万亿美元级公司的兴趣依然强劲，因为这家 ChatGPT 制造商正在寻找 2027 年的潜在产品。

paras.en: IVP's Dash said that in his AI portfolio, "a lot of companies are starting IPO prep" even if it's only "year four, year five, year six since inception." He hopes to see at least half a dozen companies go public at valuations north of $10 billion each in the second half of 2027.
paras.zh: IVP 的 Dash 表示，在他的人工智能投资组合中，“许多公司正在开始 IPO 准备”，即使这只是“自成立以来的第四年、第五年、第六年”。他希望在 2027 年下半年看到至少六家公司以每家估值超过 100 亿美元的价格上市。

paras.en: Jensen Huang's sudden departure from Nvidia has left the chip giant without a clear leader at a time when the company already faced heightened concerns about a slowdown in spending. Nvidia is a key investor in Anthropic and OpenAI and a critical supplier and financing partner for the entire AI industry, which is getting hammered across the board.
paras.zh: 黄仁勋突然从英伟达离职，导致这家芯片巨头缺乏明确的领导者，而该公司已经面临着对支出放缓的高度担忧。 Nvidia 是 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的主要投资者，也是整个人工智能行业的重要供应商和融资合作伙伴，该行业正遭受全面打击。

paras.en: In January, Democrats will take control of the House and Senate after this month's midterm elections, which included the passage of numerous ballot measures that could stymie data center development. Anthropic investor Brad Gerstner predicted after the election that market dynamics would push Anthropic to price toward the lower end of its range.
paras.zh: 1月份，民主党将在本月的中期选举后控制参众两院，其中包括通过多项可能阻碍数据中心发展的投票措施。 Anthropic 投资者布拉德·格斯特纳 (Brad Gerstner) 在大选后预测，市场动态将推动 Anthropic 的定价接近其区间的下限。

paras.en: Narasin said he wasn't even sure the company would get that far.
paras.zh: 纳拉辛表示，他甚至不确定公司能否走到这一步。

paras.en: "I was concerned they'd delay," Narasin said.
paras.zh: “我担心他们会拖延，”纳拉辛说。

paras.en: That makes the outcome that much more impressive, he said, after Anthropic priced above its expected range and upsized the offering.
paras.zh: 他表示，在 Anthropic 定价高于预期范围并扩大发行规模后，这使得结果更加令人印象深刻。

paras.en: "This will be bedtime stories for years for future VCs," Narasin said. "There was a company that was created, backed by angels and later venture" that in a few short years "became the single biggest IPO of all history."
paras.zh: “这将是未来风险投资人多年来的睡前故事，”纳拉辛说。 “有一家公司在天使和后来的风险投资的支持下成立了”，在短短几年内“成为了历史上最大的单一IPO。”

paras.en: — CNBC's Ari Levy contributed to this report.
paras.zh: — CNBC 的 Ari Levy 对本报告做出了贡献。

articles.title: Trump says there could be a 'positive spin' from the latest FBI database hack

paras.en: President Donald Trump suggested Saturday that there could be a bright spot in the latest incursion into the FBI computer database.
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统周六表示，最近一次对联邦调查局计算机数据库的入侵可能存在一个亮点。

paras.en: The president confirmed in an interview with Fox News that a system has been breached that houses information used by law enforcement at all levels to share criminal justice information.
paras.zh: 总统在接受福克斯新闻采访时证实，一个系统已被破坏，该系统保存了各级执法部门用于共享刑事司法信息的信息。

paras.en: The hackers accessed the National Criminal Information Center (NCIC), a database that includes FBI fingerprint records, wanted persons, violent felons, missing persons and related information, two people familiar with the matter told MS NOW. The database is restricted to law enforcement use but not classified and it is unclear what data was extracted.
paras.zh: 两名知情人士告诉《MS NOW》，黑客访问了国家犯罪信息中心（NCIC），该数据库包含联邦调查局指纹记录、通缉犯、暴力重罪犯、失踪人员和相关信息。该数据库仅限执法部门使用，但未分类，目前还不清楚提取了哪些数据。

paras.en: CNN had first reported on the suspected hack, citing sources familiar with the issue.
paras.zh: 美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 首先援引熟悉该问题的消息人士的话说，报道了这起疑似黑客攻击事件。

paras.en: In a wide-ranging interview on Fox, Trump said there could be upside from the news.
paras.zh: 特朗普在接受福克斯新闻采访时表示，这一消息可能会带来好处。

paras.en: "Maybe we'll learn about the voter fraud, all the voter fraud that took place," he said. "I always like to put things on a positive spin."
paras.zh: “也许我们会了解选民欺诈，所有发生过的选民欺诈，”他说。 “我总是喜欢把事情往积极的方向发展。”

paras.en: This would be the second recent intrusion into the FBI system; the previous one came in September, when a group known as "ShinyHunters" broke into an FBI jobs website. The result compromised data on current and former FBI employees and shut down part of the agency's operations until the issue was resolved.
paras.zh: 这将是 FBI 系统近期第二次遭到入侵；上一次发生在 9 月份，当时一个名为“ShinyHunters”的组织闯入了 FBI 的招聘网站。结果泄露了联邦调查局现任和前任雇员的数据，并关闭了该机构的部分业务，直到问题得到解决。

paras.en: Trump said it's possible there could be information gleaned from the latest hack.
paras.zh: 特朗普表示，有可能从最新的黑客攻击中收集到信息。

paras.en: "I wonder who's doing it, because wouldn't it be great to learn about Russia, Russia, Russia?" he said. "People should hear about it, because it actually put our country in danger, and so maybe we'll learn things that we wouldn't have learned otherwise."
paras.zh: “我想知道是谁在做这件事，因为了解俄罗斯、俄罗斯、俄罗斯不是很棒吗？”他说。 “人们应该了解它，因为它实际上使我们的国家处于危险之中，所以也许我们会学到一些我们本来不会学到的东西。”

paras.en: The FBI did not immediately respond to a CNBC request for comment.
paras.zh: FBI 没有立即回应 CNBC 的置评请求。

articles.title: Russian cargo ship hit by drones in Baltic, Finland tightens security

paras.en: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after being hit by drones in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and later drifted into Finnish waters, prompting Helsinki to impose temporary air and maritime restrictions and say Ukraine was probably behind the attack.
paras.zh: 周六，一艘俄罗斯货船在波罗的海被无人机击中后起火，随后漂入芬兰水域，促使赫尔辛基实施临时空中和海上限制，并表示乌克兰可能是此次袭击的幕后黑手。

paras.en: The Sparta II, bound for Russian exclave Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters west of Russia's Gogland island, Finland's Defence Forces said, corroborating an earlier account by Russian officials.
paras.zh: 芬兰国防军表示，前往俄罗斯飞地加里宁格勒的斯巴达二号在俄罗斯戈格兰岛以西的国际水域受损，这证实了俄罗斯官员早些时候的说法。

paras.en: "It is likely that Ukraine ... is behind (the attack)," Finnish armed forces spokesperson Aki-Mauri Huhtinen told a press conference, adding it was not clear why the vessel had been targeted.
paras.zh: 芬兰武装部队发言人 Aki-Mauri Huhtinen 在新闻发布会上表示：“乌克兰……很可能是这次袭击的幕后黑手。”他补充说，目前尚不清楚这艘船为何成为袭击目标。

paras.en: Finland's Border Guard said there was no danger to maritime traffic or people, that rescue units were at the scene, and that it was coordinating operations with neighboring countries.
paras.zh: 芬兰边防卫队表示，海上交通或人员没有危险，救援部队已在现场，并正在与邻国协调行动。

paras.en: Gulf of Finland coast guard commander Mikko Simola later told a press conference that the vessel had anchored, and its crew was evacuating.
paras.zh: 芬兰湾海岸警卫队指挥官米科·西莫拉后来在新闻发布会上表示，该船已经抛锚，船员正在撤离。

paras.en: Helsinki said it had introduced temporary aviation and maritime restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland to protect civilians and allow authorities to operate if drones needed to be intercepted.
paras.zh: 赫尔辛基表示，已在芬兰湾东部实行临时航空和海上限制，以保护平民，并允许当局在需要拦截无人机时采取行动。

paras.en: "The war is spilling over into our neighboring areas. Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said on X.
paras.zh: 芬兰总理佩特里·奥尔波 (Petteri Orpo) 在 X 台上表示：“战争正在蔓延到我们的邻近地区。芬兰当局正在处理芬兰湾的局势，一艘无人机袭击了那里的一艘俄罗斯商船。乌克兰有权打击侵略者。”

paras.en: Ukraine's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
paras.zh: 乌克兰外交部没有立即回应置评请求。

paras.en: Russia's embassy in Helsinki did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯驻赫尔辛基大使馆没有立即回应置评请求。

paras.en: The vessel is subject to US sanctions and is linked to Russian shipping company Oboronlogistika, according to the U.S. Treasury Department.
paras.zh: 据美国财政部称，该船受到美国制裁，并与俄罗斯航运公司 Oboronlogisticika 有关。

paras.en: Oboronlogistika provides logistics services for the Russian defense ministry, according to the company's website.
paras.zh: 据该公司网站称，Oboronlogisticika 为俄罗斯国防部提供后勤服务。

paras.en: "At the moment, there is no confirmed information about what cargo is on board, but it cannot be ruled out that there is military materiel on board," Finnish Border Guard Commander Ilja Iljin told Reuters.
paras.zh: 芬兰边防卫队指挥官伊尔贾·伊尔金（Ilja Iljin）对路透社表示：“目前还没有关于船上载有什么货物的确认信息，但不能排除船上有军用物资。”

paras.en: Helsinki said separately that a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating Finnish airspace on Saturday, possibly in connection with rescue or monitoring operations involving the damaged vessel.
paras.zh: 赫尔辛基另外表示，一架俄罗斯直升机涉嫌于周六侵犯芬兰领空，可能与受损船只的救援或监测行动有关。

paras.en: Leningrad region Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said on Telegram that a cargo vessel had been attacked by two drones in international waters about 3 nautical miles from Russia's border. He did not identify the vessel.
paras.zh: 列宁格勒地区州长亚历山大·德罗兹登科在 Telegram 上表示，一艘货船在距俄罗斯边境约 3 海里的国际水域遭到两架无人机袭击。他没有透露这艘船的身份。

paras.en: Drozdenko also said 80 drones had been shot down over the Leningrad region overnight.
paras.zh: 德罗兹登科还表示，一夜之间，列宁格勒地区上空有 80 架无人机被击落。

paras.en: Finland's military said last week it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area during a wave of Ukrainian drone attacks on the Leningrad region.
paras.zh: 芬兰军方上周表示，在乌克兰无人机对列宁格勒地区发动一波袭击期间，在同一地区发现一艘俄罗斯军舰遭到袭击。

paras.en: Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said on X his country was monitoring the situation and had offered assistance to Finland, without providing details.
paras.zh: 瑞典首相乌尔夫·克里斯特森 (Ulf Kristersson) 10 日表示，瑞典正在关注事态发展，并向芬兰提供援助，但未提供细节。

paras.en: Estonia's Police and Border Guard Board said in an emailed statement that preliminary information indicated there had been explosions on board the Sparta II, and that it was also monitoring the situation.
paras.zh: 爱沙尼亚警察和边防局在一份电子邮件声明中表示，初步信息显示“斯巴达二号”船上发生爆炸，该局也在监视事态发展。

paras.en: Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said the incident posed no threat to supplies to the region.
paras.zh: 加里宁格勒州长阿列克谢·贝斯普罗兹万内赫表示，这一事件对该地区的供应没有构成威胁。

paras.en: Kaliningrad, which lies between Poland and Lithuania, has periodically been a flashpoint between Russia and NATO and the European Union.
paras.zh: 加里宁格勒位于波兰和立陶宛之间，经常成为俄罗斯与北约和欧盟之间的冲突点。

paras.en: Russia has previously described attacks on its commercial vessels outside its territorial waters as acts of terrorism and maritime piracy.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯此前曾将在其领海之外对其商船的袭击描述为恐怖主义和海盗行为。

paras.en: The Sparta II is a 121-meter (397-foot) Russian-flagged cargo vessel owned by Oboronlogistika that left St Petersburg on Friday, according to LSEG data.
paras.zh: 根据 LSEG 的数据，Sparta II 是一艘 121 米（397 英尺）长、悬挂俄罗斯国旗的货船，由 Oboronlogisticika 拥有，于周五离开圣彼得堡。

paras.en: The Gulf of Finland is a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea between Finland and Estonia that extends east to St Petersburg. Gogland lies in the eastern Gulf of Finland, about 40 km (25 miles) from Finland's coast.
paras.zh: 芬兰湾是芬兰和爱沙尼亚之间波罗的海的狭窄海湾，向东延伸至圣彼得堡。戈格兰位于芬兰湾东部，距芬兰海岸约 40 公里（25 英里）。

articles.title: Our solar system’s doomsday may come sooner than we thought

paras.en: I’m starting to really wonder just how stable our solar system really is.
paras.zh: 我开始真正想知道我们的太阳系到底有多稳定。

paras.en: To be clear, I’m not worried about planets being flung away into interstellar space any time soon. But “soon” means something different to an astronomer than it does to a normal person. Millions of years is “soon.” A few billion? Now that’s a bit later.
paras.zh: 需要明确的是，我并不担心行星很快就会被抛入星际空间。但“很快”对于天文学家和普通人来说意味着不同的东西。数百万年“很快”。几十亿？现在那是有点晚了。

paras.en: Fail to factor in deep time, though, and it’s all too easy to mistakenly think that the solar system is static, that it has always been as it is now. After all, it looks well ordered. The inner four planets are all small and rocky, while the outer four are swollen giants with thick atmospheres, and a belt of asteroids splits the two types like a demarcation zone.
paras.zh: 然而，如果不考虑深度时间，就很容易错误地认为太阳系是静态的，它一直都是现在的样子。毕竟，看起来秩序井然。里面的四颗行星都是小而多岩石的，而外面的四颗是肿胀的巨行星，有着厚厚的大气层，一条小行星带像分界线一样将这两种类型分开。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: But things are not as they appear. One clue turned up when astronomers found the first exoplanets orbiting sunlike stars in the 1990s. These were “hot Jupiters,” gas giants akin to our solar system’s biggest planet but huddled in orbits far closer to their stars than Mercury is to our own. They could not have formed there, so astronomers postulated they were instead born farther out and gradually migrated inward via gravitational interactions with the same circumstellar disk of material from which they first coalesced.
paras.zh: 但事情并不像看上去的那样。当天文学家在 20 世纪 90 年代发现第一批绕类日恒星运行的系外行星时，一条线索出现了。这些是“热木星”，类似于我们太阳系最大行星的气态巨行星，但它们挤在离恒星更近的轨道上，比水星离我们自己的轨道更近。它们不可能在那里形成，因此天文学家假设它们诞生于更远的地方，并通过与它们最初合并的同一个星周物质盘的引力相互作用逐渐向内迁移。

paras.en: The hot Jupiters were only an early wave of weird worlds. In some other systems, planets orbit on wildly tilted trajectories, and, here and there, astronomers have found planets that actually revolve around their host stars backward. These oddities imply some sort of chaotic interaction at work, such as planets perturbing each other as they pass by and getting tossed into bizarre configurations.
paras.zh: 炽热的木星只是奇怪世界的早期浪潮。在其他一些系统中，行星沿着极度倾斜的轨道运行，天文学家到处都发现了实际上向后围绕其主恒星旋转的行星。这些奇怪的现象意味着工作中存在某种混乱的相互作用，例如行星经过时相互扰动并陷入奇怪的配置。

paras.en: Then, in 2005, scientists proposed what is now called the Nice model (after the French city where the scientists met and developed the idea). This radical hypothesis is that the solar system’s giant planets formed closer to the sun than their present positions, only to migrate outward to their current arrangement as a result of gravitational tussles with each other. The Nice model, and its many subsequent modifications, brought the “migratory” view of planets home, and this key insight has been a staple of solar system dynamics ever since.
paras.zh: 然后，在 2005 年，科学家们提出了现在所谓的尼斯模型（以科学家们相遇并提出这一想法的法国城市命名）。这个激进的假设是，太阳系的巨型行星形成时比它们现在的位置更靠近太阳，只是由于彼此的引力争斗而向外迁移到它们当前的排列。尼斯模型及其随后的许多修改，将行星的“迁移”观点带回了家，从那时起，这一关键见解就一直是太阳系动力学的主要内容。

paras.en: I consider planetary migration’s place in celestial mechanics as similar to the role of evolution in biology or plate tectonics in geology: nothing makes sense unless you include it. It’s the framework of how we understand the way planetary orbits evolve.
paras.zh: 我认为行星迁移在天体力学中的地位类似于生物学中进化论或地质学中板块构造的作用：除非你把它包括在内，否则没有任何意义。它是我们理解行星轨道演化方式的框架。

paras.en: It also strongly implies these changes are ongoing. The solar system continues to evolve.
paras.zh: 这也强烈暗示这些变化正在进行中。太阳系继续演化。

paras.en: In one sense, we already knew this to be true: The sun won’t last forever. As I wrote in my September 18, 2026, Universe column, in six billion years or so, changes in our star’s core will lead to it swelling up and becoming a red giant. The puffed-up sun will slowly shed its outer layers, causing its mass to decrease and its gravity to weaken, and in response, the planets will gradually move farther out from it. Some astronomers had previously assumed that this relatively gentle process meant the outer solar system planets would orbit stably for immense periods of time, possibly as much as 100 billion years—long after the sun itself is quite dead.
paras.zh: 从某种意义上说，我们已经知道这是真的：太阳不会永远存在。正如我在 2026 年 9 月 18 日的宇宙专栏中所写，在大约 60 亿年的时间里，我们恒星核心的变化将导致它膨胀并成为红巨星。膨胀的太阳会慢慢地脱落其外层，导致其质量减少，引力减弱，作为回应，行星将逐渐远离它。一些天文学家此前认为，这种相对温和的过程意味着太阳系外行星将在很长一段时间内稳定地运行，可能长达 1000 亿年——在太阳本身完全死亡之后很久。

paras.en: There’s evidence that suggests the sun’s future evolution won’t be a smooth, sedate process, though: instabilities in its core will result in episodic paroxysms in which our star’s luminosity will briefly increase drastically. These sporadic stellar spasms will cause the sun to lose mass in powerful but brief pulses instead of in a smooth flow.
paras.zh: 不过，有证据表明，太阳未来的演化不会是一个平稳、平静的过程：其核心的不稳定将导致偶发性的发作，其中我们恒星的光度将短暂急剧增加。这些零星的恒星痉挛将导致太阳以强大但短暂的脉冲而不是平稳的流动方式失去质量。

paras.en: And there’s more: research into how the sun loses that mass shows that it won’t be blown off symmetrically in all directions. Instead each pulse will send material off asymmetrically, in a relatively random direction, like a sudden gust of wind.
paras.zh: 还有更多：对太阳如何失去质量的研究表明，它不会在各个方向上对称地被吹走。相反，每个脉冲都会以相对随机的方向不对称地发送物质，就像突然的一阵风一样。

paras.en: If this is indeed the case, it will a have profound impact on the far future of the solar system.
paras.zh: 如果情况确实如此，这将对太阳系遥远的未来产生深远的影响。

paras.en: A team of astronomers looked into this and published its results on September 21 in the Astrophysical Journal Letters. The researchers simulated how the sun will lose mass over the course of several billion years—from when it starts to become a red giant to the inevitable end of the process, in which it loses all its outer layers, exposing its core to space. At that point it will be a white dwarf, a hot, dense ball with about half the current solar mass but squeezed into a volume only about the size of Earth.
paras.zh: 一组天文学家对此进行了研究，并于 9 月 21 日在《天体物理学杂志快报》上发表了研究结果。研究人员模拟了太阳在数十亿年的过程中如何失去质量——从它开始变成红巨星到这个过程不可避免的结束，在这个过程中它失去了所有的外层，将其核心暴露在太空中。到那时，它将成为一颗白矮星，一颗炽热而致密的球体，质量约为当前太阳质量的一半，但体积却被压缩到只有地球大小。

paras.en: In their simulations, they assumed that the solar mass loss will occur in a series of thousands of small burps, each one ejecting about 0.01 percent of the sun’s material into space. Also, these solar eructations will form a broad funnel shape instead of expanding spherically.
paras.zh: 在他们的模拟中，他们假设太阳质量损失将在一系列数千个小打嗝中发生，每个小打嗝都会将大约 0.01% 的太阳物质喷射到太空中。此外，这些太阳喷发将形成一个宽阔的漏斗形状，而不是球形扩张。

paras.en: That last bit is critical. By focusing the emitted material, the ejection acts like a rocket, pushing on the sun. The amount of force imparted is relatively small, only enough to give it a very small kick. But this does accelerate our star, each adding a few meters per second to its velocity in space.
paras.zh: 最后一点很关键。通过聚焦发射的物质，喷射就像火箭一样，推动太阳。施加的力量相对较小，只够给它一个很小的踢击。但这确实加速了我们的恒星，每每秒增加几米的太空速度。

paras.en: Each kick is in a random direction. Now, you might think this would average out to zero net force acting on the sun, but that’s not the case. This situation mimics that of a “random walk,” in which taking a step in a random direction slowly leads away from your starting point. After a finite number of steps, you’ll have moved in some direction as if pushed there. In the same way, random ejections of matter can push a star in some overall direction as well, leading to the final velocity of several kilometers per second.
paras.zh: 每次踢球的方向都是随机的。现在，您可能认为作用在太阳上的净力平均为零，但事实并非如此。这种情况类似于“随机行走”，即朝随机方向迈出一步，慢慢远离起点。经过有限的步数后，你会朝着某个方向移动，就像被推到那里一样。同样，物质的随机喷射也可以将恒星推向某个整体方向，导致最终速度达到每秒几公里。

paras.en: This may not seem like much, but it will actually have a big effect on the planets.
paras.zh: 这看起来可能不多，但实际上会对行星产生很大的影响。

paras.en: Well, not the inner planets so much—we already know what happens to them, and it’s nothing good. Mercury and Venus will be consumed by the expanding sun. Earth may escape that fate, but both it and Mars will be broiled as our star grows enormous.
paras.zh: 好吧，内行星就不那么重要了——我们已经知道它们会发生什么，但这没什么好处。水星和金星将被膨胀的太阳吞噬。地球可能会逃脱这种命运，但随着我们的恒星变得巨大，它和火星都将被烤焦。

paras.en: But, according to the new work, the outer planets don’t fare much better.
paras.zh: 但是，根据这项新研究，外行星的情况也好不到哪儿去。

paras.en: In practical terms, as these kicks push around the sun, the planets’ orbits around it become more elongated. In a disturbing 77 percent of the simulations, the outer planets migrate so much because of this mass loss that eventually one crosses the orbit of another—and this happens early on in the process. In at least one case, Saturn is lost within just a few million years of the sun becoming a red giant! These gravitational encounters lead to ejected planets or system disruptions in 40 percent of the simulations, long before the sun even becomes a white dwarf. After three billion years, total disruption occurs in a staggering 90 percent of the simulations.
paras.zh: 实际上，当这些踢力围绕太阳运行时，行星围绕太阳的轨道变得更加拉长。在 77% 的模拟中，令人不安的是，外行星由于质量损失而发生大量迁移，最终导致一颗行星穿过另一颗行星的轨道，而这种情况发生在这一过程的早期。至少在一种情况下，土星在太阳变成红巨星后的短短几百万年内就消失了！在 40% 的模拟中，这些引力相遇会导致行星喷射或系统中断，甚至早在太阳变成白矮星之前就已经发生了。三十亿年后，令人震惊的是，90% 的模拟都发生了彻底的破坏。

paras.en: Previously astronomers thought that as the sun died and the orbits of the planets expanded, nearby passes of other stars would eventually disrupt the solar system after many tens of billions of years. This new work indicates that by the time these close encounters happen, there won’t be much of a solar system left to disrupt.
paras.zh: 此前天文学家认为，随着太阳死亡和行星轨道扩张，附近其他恒星的经过最终会在数百亿年后扰乱太阳系。这项新研究表明，当这些近距离接触发生时，太阳系将不再有太多可以破坏的地方。

paras.en: That’s a little depressing. If there’s an upside, it’s that this won’t happen for many billions of years from now. As far as we can tell, the planets—including our own—will be fine for eons to come.
paras.zh: 这有点令人沮丧。如果说有什么好处的话，那就是这种情况在数十亿年后都不会发生。据我们所知，行星——包括我们自己的行星——在未来的亿万年里都将保持良好状态。

paras.en: But if you have plans for seven or eight billion years hence, you might want to reassess them.
paras.zh: 但如果你有七八十亿年的计划，你可能需要重新评估它们。

articles.title: What do other planets smell like? The answer hides in their chemistry

paras.en: Humanity has long looked up and yearned to know more about the glowing dots in the night sky. Over the past century, advances in technology have allowed us to glean amazingly good insights into both distant stars and our closest cosmic neighbors. But while high-tech probes may tell us what the atmosphere is like on Jupiter, Saturn or Mars, we still can’t directly answer one deceptively simple question: What does it smell like on other planets?
paras.zh: 人类长期以来一直仰望并渴望更多地了解夜空中的发光点。在过去的一个世纪里，技术的进步使我们能够对遥远的恒星和我们最近的宇宙邻居获得令人惊讶的良好见解。尽管高科技探测器可能会告诉我们木星、土星或火星上的大气层是什么样的，但我们仍然无法直接回答一个看似简单的问题：其他行星上的大气层闻起来像什么？

paras.en: A human may not ever make it to another planet to sniff for themselves. But scientists do have some ideas of such worlds’ odor—albeit rough ones. That’s because astronomers use tools called spectroscopes, which measure how different gases affect the wavelength of light, as well as sampling probes and models of gravity and density, to work out which elements are present on the planets. Some of those elements smell in specific ways.
paras.zh: 人类可能永远无法到达另一个星球来进行自我嗅觉。但科学家们确实对此类世界的气味有一些想法——尽管很粗糙。这是因为天文学家使用称为分光镜的工具来测量不同气体如何影响光的波长，以及采样探针和重力和密度模型，以计算出行星上存在哪些元素。其中一些元素具有特定的气味。

paras.en: But while we know those chemical signatures are there, few have given much thought to how they might translate to human senses. In that regard, Boyko Ranguelov may be unique. A physics professor at Bulgaria’s University of Mining and Geology, Ranguelov has long been interested in what he calls the planets’ “organoleptic properties,” or how the worlds would stimulate human senses.
paras.zh: 尽管我们知道这些化学特征的存在，但很少有人认真思考它们如何转化为人类的感官。在这方面，博伊科·兰格洛夫可能是独一无二的。兰格洛夫是保加利亚矿业和地质大学的物理学教授，长期以来一直对他所说的行星的“感官特性”感兴趣，或者说行星如何刺激人类的感官。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “The combination of these properties are exciting to me, as I’m interested by unusual phenomena,” he says.
paras.zh: “这些特性的结合令我兴奋，因为我对不寻常的现象很感兴趣，”他说。

paras.en: In a 2022 presentation to Bulgarian and Serbian astronomers, Ranguelov laid out his theories of what the other planets in the solar system smell like. The gas giants largely smell terrible, he says, like rotten eggs or human farts. That’s because of the dominant chemicals of hydrogen, helium, hydrogen sulfide, ammonia, phosphine, hydrogen cyanide and ammonium hydrosulfide. That terrible smell would only be amplified by the high pressures that exist lower in their atmospheres.
paras.zh: 在 2022 年向保加利亚和塞尔维亚天文学家发表的演讲中，兰格洛夫阐述了他关于太阳系其他行星气味的理论。他说，这些气态巨行星的气味非常难闻，就像臭鸡蛋或人类的屁一样。这是因为主要化学物质是氢、氦、硫化氢、氨、磷化氢、氰化氢和硫氢化铵。这种可怕的气味只会因大气层较低处存在的高压而放大。

paras.en: “According to our human senses, the other space bodies in our solar system are not very friendly,” Ranguelov says. “We are strongly accommodated to Earth’s smells and would be badly surprised to smell other space bodies.”
paras.zh: “根据我们人类的感觉，太阳系中的其他太空天体并不是很友好，”兰格洛夫说。 “我们非常适应地球的气味，如果闻到其他太空天体的味道，我们会感到非常惊讶。”

paras.en: Rocky planets, such as Mars or Venus, are different. Because of the amount of iron present on Mars, it likely smells similar to rust, with a hint of gunpowder, Ranguelov says.
paras.zh: 岩石行星，例如火星或金星，则不同。兰格洛夫说，由于火星上存在大量的铁，它的气味可能类似于铁锈，并带有一丝火药味。

paras.en: While there may not be any direct knowledge of planetary smells, there are a tiny handful of humans who have indirectly smelled another celestial object. Apollo astronauts who landed on the moon reported that their equipment and samples had a distinct odor.
paras.zh: 虽然可能没有任何关于行星气味的直接知识，但有一小部分人间接闻到了另一个天体的气味。登陆月球的阿波罗宇航员报告说，他们的设备和样品有明显的气味。

paras.en: “The samples smelled as safety matches immediately after they were collected,” according to Ranguelov. “Sometime later they lost the smell after the contact with the oxygen in the moon module cabin.”
paras.zh: 兰格洛夫表示：“这些样本在采集后立即闻起来有安全火柴的味道。” “过了一段时间，它们在接触登月舱舱内的氧气后就失去了气味。”

paras.en: If we ever venture beyond our solar system, humans may be pleasantly surprised at some of the aromas we’d find. There are indications, for example, that the molecular cloud Sagittarius B2 “will smell like an alcoholic cocktail of vodka and sour cherry liquor and salad of pickled cucumbers,” Ranguelov says. “But to get this smell, we’ll need a nose the size of several light-years.”
paras.zh: 如果我们冒险超越太阳系，人类可能会对我们发现的一些气味感到惊喜。例如，有迹象表明，人马座 B2 分子云“闻起来像伏特加、酸樱桃酒和腌黄瓜沙拉的酒精鸡尾酒，”兰格洛夫说。 “但是为了获得这种气味，我们需要一个几光年大小的鼻子。”

articles.title: Weirdly accelerating space rock keeps puzzling astronomers

paras.en: On November 16 officials from the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) announced that their Hayabusa2 spacecraft will no longer visit a small, rapidly rotating and mysteriously accelerating space rock called 1998 KY26. Operating well past its nominal lifetime, the probe is now in an “extended mission.” But as a result of problems with its engines, it couldn’t reach this object for an intended rendezvous in 2031. Instead Hayabusa2 will now visit a different target, the near-Earth asteroid 2015 BM510, in 2028.
paras.zh: 11 月 16 日，日本宇宙航空研究开发机构 (JAXA) 的官员宣布，他们的隼鸟 2 号航天器将不再访问一颗名为 1998 KY26 的小型、快速旋转且神秘加速的太空岩石。该探测器的运行时间已超过其标称使用寿命，目前正处于“延长任务”状态。但由于发动机出现问题，它无法在 2031 年到达这个目标。相反，隼鸟 2 号现在将在 2028 年访问另一个目标，即近地小行星 2015 BM510。

paras.en: In recent years, 1998 KY26 has certainly attracted an inordinate amount of attention from space scientists and the interested public alike because of its mysterious nongravitationalacceleration—that is, an acceleration that couldn’t be explained by the gravitational influence of other objects in the solar system and must have been driven by something else. I led a team that identified this object’s odd motion in 2022. Some have speculated that this anomalous movement could be a clue that 1998 KY26 isn’t a space rock at all but rather some sort of technological artifact—perhaps even the long-lost Soviet spacecraft Phobos 1.
paras.zh: 近年来，1998 KY26 无疑吸引了太空科学家和感兴趣的公众的过度关注，因为它具有神秘的非重力加速度——也就是说，这种加速度无法用太阳系中其他物体的重力影响来解释，而一定是由其他东西驱动的。我领导的团队在 2022 年识别出了这个物体的奇怪运动。一些人推测，这种异常运动可能是一个线索，表明 1998 KY26 根本不是一块太空岩石，而是某种技术制品，甚至可能是失踪已久的苏联航天器火卫一号。

paras.en: There’s a lot to unpack here, but the gist is that 1998 KY26 is indeed challenging our understanding of comets and asteroids—and has been for several years.
paras.zh: 这里有很多东西需要解开，但要点是 1998 KY26 确实挑战了我们对彗星和小行星的理解——而且已经持续了好几年了。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: A nongravitational acceleration alone isn’t necessarily cause for invoking a spacecraft; we routinely measure such effects on comets and asteroids alike. When comets get close to the sun, ices heat up and sublimate from their surfaces as vapor, producing a rocketlike (and distinctly nongravitational) recoil. The escaping vapor also usually lofts sunlight-reflecting dust along with it, creating the beautiful tails we associate with comets.
paras.zh: 非重力加速度本身并不一定是调用航天器的原因；我们经常测量彗星和小行星上的这种影响。当彗星接近太阳时，冰会升温并以蒸气的形式从其表面升华，产生火箭般的（并且明显是非重力的）反冲力。逸出的蒸气通常还会伴随着反射阳光的尘埃，形成我们与彗星联系在一起的美丽尾巴。

paras.en: Asteroids don’t have tails and presumably don’t have much ice, but we do measure similar, albeit weaker, accelerations on them, too. These are a consequence of subtler effects that all boil down to sunlight either pushing on them or unevenly heating their surfaces.
paras.zh: 小行星没有尾巴，大概也没有太多冰，但我们也测量到了类似的加速度，尽管较弱。这些都是微妙影响的结果，这些影响都归结为阳光照射在它们上或不均匀地加热它们的表面。

paras.en: But as is so often the case in nature, not all so-called minor bodies comfortably fit in our tidy, simple “comet or asteroid” categorization. In fact, in recent years Davide Farnocchia of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory and I led three papers reporting the discovery of almost 20 objects in our solar system that blur this line in a new way. These “dark comets” have properties from both comets and asteroids; they have nongravitational accelerations stronger than those of typical asteroids but exhibit no tails—or rather they showed no tails when we first detected their mysterious movements.
paras.zh: 但正如自然界中经常发生的情况一样，并非所有所谓的小天体都适合我们整洁、简单的“彗星或小行星”分类。事实上，近年来，我和 NASA 喷气推进实验室的 Davide Farnocchia 领导了三篇论文，报告了在太阳系中发现了近 20 个天体，这些天体以新的方式模糊了这条界限。这些“暗彗星”同时具有彗星和小行星的特性；它们的非重力加速度比典型的小行星更强，但没有尾巴——或者更确切地说，当我们第一次探测到它们神秘的运动时，它们没有尾巴。

paras.en: The more of these dark comets that we find, the clearer we see a telltale trend. In 2024 I led a paper that showed that they seem to be divided into two different populations: outer and inner dark comets (shown in the red and gray orbits, respectively, in the image above). The outer ones are much larger and have more elliptical orbits, while the inner ones are smaller and closer to Earth, with more circular orbits. The latter include 1998 KY26, and its relative proximity to our planet was one of the reasons it became a target for Hayabusa2; for a time, it seemed like that mission would eventually be what solved the mystery of dark comets.
paras.zh: 我们发现的暗彗星越多，我们就越清楚地看到一个明显的趋势。 2024 年，我领导了一篇论文，表明它们似乎分为两个不同的种群：外部暗彗星和内部暗彗星（分别在上图中的红色和灰色轨道中显示）。外层的卫星更大，轨道更多为椭圆形，而内层的轨道更小，更靠近地球，轨道更多为圆形。后者包括 1998 KY26，它与地球的相对距离是它成为隼鸟 2 号目标的原因之一；有一段时间，这项任务似乎最终将解开黑暗彗星之谜。

paras.en: Now, of course, the situation is more complicated.
paras.zh: 当然，现在的情况更加复杂了。

paras.en: Within the last year, we finally snapped images of cometary tails on two of the known outer dark comets, confirming that cometary venting was causing their mysterious motion. Meanwhile telescope data have revealed that 1998 KY26 is significantly smaller than previously thought, and Farnocchia led a study that showed how, given this smaller size, the effects of sunlight alone could explain 1998 KY26’s motion. And a couple of weeks ago Korbin Hansen and Masatoshi Hirabayashi, both at the Georgia Institute of Technology, published another study showing that 1998 KY26 is probably too warm to sustain ice, lending more credence to the updated radiation model from Farnocchia and his colleagues.
paras.zh: 去年，我们终于在两颗已知的外暗彗星上拍摄到了彗尾的图像，证实了彗星喷发导致了它们神秘的运动。与此同时，望远镜数据显示 1998 KY26 比之前认为的要小得多，Farnocchia 领导的一项研究表明，鉴于尺寸较小，仅靠阳光的影响就可以解释 1998 KY26 的运动。几周前，佐治亚理工学院的 Korbin Hansen 和 Masatoshi Hirabayashi 发表了另一项研究，表明 1998 年 KY26 可能太温暖，无法维持冰，这为 Farnocchia 和他的同事更新的辐射模型提供了更多可信度。

paras.en: None of this proves that 1998 KY26 isn’t some derelict spacecraft. On the contrary, given that cometlike venting of vapor probably doesn’t explain the motion of 1998 KY26, it could be argued that, by extension, this weakens that explanation for other inner dark comets, too. Then again, in the past some researchers have argued that other dark comets were defunct spacecraft as well, but these claims were quickly shown to be incorrect. While it would be a remarkable development if some of the dark comets turned out to be spacecraft, we have plausible explanations for all of their motions.
paras.zh: 所有这些都不能证明 1998 KY26 不是一些废弃的航天器。相反，鉴于类似彗星的蒸汽排出可能无法解释 1998 KY26 的运动，因此可以说，推而广之，这也削弱了对其他内部暗彗星的解释。话又说回来，过去一些研究人员认为其他暗彗星也是报废的航天器，但这些说法很快就被证明是不正确的。如果一些暗彗星被证明是航天器，那将是一个了不起的发展，但我们对它们的所有运动都有合理的解释。

paras.en: It is disappointing that Hayabusa2 won’t be visiting 1998 KY26, but the reasons for this have nothing to do with this object being anything besides an admittedly weird space rock. The reality is that the updated radiation-force model tracks with the best available measurements that indicate 1998 KY26’s reduced size, potentially obviating the need for more off-beat interpretations.
paras.zh: 令人失望的是隼鸟 2 号不会访问 1998 KY26，但其原因与该物体除了是一块公认的奇怪的太空岩石之外没有任何关系。现实情况是，更新后的辐射力模型跟踪了最佳可用测量结果，表明 1998 KY26 尺寸减小，从而可能消除对更多异常解释的需要。

paras.en: And still a beguiling mystery remains: the emerging picture in this rapidly developing field is that dark comets really are divided into two distinct populations. These outer objects seem to be covert comets disguising themselves as innocuous asteroids, while the inner ones are something else entirely, forcing us to rethink how radiation forces work in the solar system’s asteroids. The solar system—and the dark comets it contains—keeps presenting us with new puzzles.
paras.zh: 仍然存在一个令人迷惑的谜团：在这个快速发展的领域中出现的情况是，暗彗星实际上分为两个不同的种群。这些外部天体似乎是隐藏的彗星，伪装成无害的小行星，而内部天体则完全是另一回事，迫使我们重新思考辐射力在太阳系小行星中的作用。太阳系及其所包含的黑暗彗星不断向我们提出新的谜题。

paras.en: This is an opinion and analysis article, and the views expressed by the author or authors are not necessarily those of Scientific American.
paras.zh: 这是一篇观点和分析文章，作者表达的观点并不一定代表《科学美国人》的观点。

articles.title: American science is broken. Meet the people fixing it
articles.author: Hannah Richter

paras.en: The February sun was setting outside her family’s West Virginia home when Rebecca Lindsey found out she was being fired in 75 minutes. Lindsey, who until early 2025 managed the federal government’s climate.gov website, had just begun to think her job might be safe during the second Trump administration.
paras.zh: 当丽贝卡·林赛 (Rebecca Lindsey) 75 分钟后发现自己将被解雇时，二月的太阳正在她位于西弗吉尼亚州的家外落下。林赛在 2025 年初之前一直负责管理联邦政府的 Climate.gov 网站，她刚刚开始认为在特朗普第二届政府期间她的工作可能会很安全。

paras.en: “Every week, it was like, ‘This is the week we’re all going to get fired,’ ” says Lindsey, who had worked as a contractor and later a civil servant at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration for nearly 15 years. “Every time you would hear the rumor and then it wouldn’t happen, you would think … maybe this is all just talk.”
paras.zh: “每一周，我们都会感觉‘这周我们都会被解雇’，”林赛说，他曾在国家海洋和大气管理局担任承包商，后来担任公务员近 15 年。 “每次你听到谣言，然后这件事并没有发生，你就会想……也许这只是说说而已。”

paras.en: But at 3:45 p.m. on February 27, 2025, Lindsey and around 800 of her NOAA colleagues received a mass termination email saying they no longer “fit the Agency’s current needs.” In June, Lindsey’s sister and the data visualization lead for the project, Mary Lindsey, was fired alongside the remaining climate.gov contractors. The website URL was redirected, hiding the site — and its decades’ worth of climate visualizations, educational tools and extreme weather trackers — from the public.
paras.zh: 但下午 3 点 45 分2025 年 2 月 27 日，Lindsey 和约 800 名 NOAA 同事收到一封大规模解雇电子邮件，称他们不再“符合该机构当前的需求”。六月，Lindsey 的妹妹兼该项目的数据可视化负责人 Mary Lindsey 与其余的 Climate.gov 承包商一起被解雇。该网站的 URL 被重定向，向公众隐藏了该网站及其数十年的气候可视化、教育工具和极端天气跟踪器。

paras.en: The Lindsey sisters decided to fight back. Along with another terminated NOAA employee, they split a $65,000 grant from the nonprofit Surge Climate Talent and launched a crowdfunding campaign to rebuild and update climate.gov. The site, now called climate.us, notched one million views in its first month.
paras.zh: 林赛姐妹决定反击。他们与另一名被 NOAA 解雇的员工一起，分享了非营利组织 Surge Climate Talent 提供的 65,000 美元赠款，并发起了一项众筹活动，以重建和更新 Climate.gov。该网站现名为 Climate.us，上线第一个月就获得了 100 万次浏览量。

paras.en: But as proud as they are of their work, the project is a patch, not a fix. Rebecca Lindsey predicts it would take at least seven employees and $1.8 million annually to resume 80 percent of the old site’s work. “Climate.gov was more than just a website; it was a climate literacy program,” she says. To rescue the full mission, they still have a long way to go.
paras.zh: 尽管他们对自己的工作感到自豪，但该项目只是一个补丁，而不是修复。丽贝卡·林赛 (Rebecca Lindsey) 预计，每年至少需要 7 名员工和 180 万美元才能恢复旧站点 80% 的工作。 “Climate.gov 不仅仅是一个网站；它还是一个气候知识项目，”她说。要想完成完整的救援任务，他们还有很长的路要走。

paras.en: The Lindsey sisters are far from the only tale of makeshift resilience. Over the last year, untold numbers of U.S. scientists and their supporters have rebuilt data dashboards, formed recommendation groups for childhood vaccines and screenings, and doled out research funds for hundreds of stranded early-career scientists. They’ve reconstituted committees to advise space missions, rehomed key reports on climate and Arctic science, and even turned to social media to spread public health alerts in the wake of a massive realignment of the federal science enterprise.
paras.zh: 林赛姐妹并不是唯一一个临时恢复的故事。去年，无数美国科学家及其支持者重建了数据仪表板，成立了儿童疫苗和筛查推荐小组，并为数百名陷入困境的早期职业科学家发放了研究资金。他们重组了委员会来为太空任务提供建议，重新调整有关气候和北极科学的重要报告，甚至在联邦科学事业大规模重组后利用社交媒体来传播公共卫生警报。

paras.en: “I don’t think anyone could have foreseen the amount of destruction and deliberate breaking down of norms and infrastructure” over the last two years, says Christina Madison, a clinical pharmacist and public health communicator known on social media as The Public Health Pharmacist.
paras.zh: 在社交媒体上被称为“公共卫生药剂师”的临床药剂师和公共卫生传播者克里斯蒂娜·麦迪逊（Christina Madison）表示，“我认为没有人能够预见到过去两年中破坏的程度以及对规范和基础设施的故意破坏”。

paras.en: Since January 2025, the second Trump administration has frozen or rescinded billions of dollars in research funding on topics from climate change to vaccine hesitancy and is trying to redirect it — often without congressional approval — to administration priorities such as artificial intelligence and quantum computing. During deliberations for the FY2026 and FY2027 budgets, the White House proposed slashing future science funding by one-third.
paras.zh: 自 2025 年 1 月以来，特朗普第二届政府冻结或取消了数十亿美元的研究经费，涉及气候变化、疫苗犹豫等话题，并试图将其（通常未经国会批准）转向人工智能和量子计算等政府优先事项。在审议 2026 财年和 2027 财年预算时，白宫提议将未来的科学经费削减三分之一。

paras.en: “When this was first starting, it really, truly felt like an alternate universe,” says Sean O’Leary, a pediatric infectious disease researcher at the University of Colorado Anschutz. “The science was always what drove the decision making, and now we’re at a place where it’s not.”
paras.zh: 科罗拉多大学安舒茨分校的儿科传染病研究员肖恩·奥利里 (Sean O’Leary) 表示：“当这一切刚开始时，真的感觉就像是另一个宇宙。” “科学始终是推动决策的因素，但现在我们却处于一个并非如此的境地。”

paras.en: In 2025 alone, the federal government shed some 20 percent
paras.zh: 仅 2025 年，联邦政府就削减了约 20%

paras.en: of its science workforce. And in May 2026, the Office of Management and Budget proposed a sweeping set of rules to expand the authority of federal political appointees in selecting science grants.
paras.zh: 其科学劳动力。 2026 年 5 月，管理和预算办公室提出了一套全面的规则，以扩大联邦政治任命人员在选择科学拨款方面的权力。

paras.en: Approximate proportion of the scientific workforce who left federal service in 2025
paras.zh: 2025 年离开联邦服务的科学工作者的大致比例

paras.en: Yet some researchers see the destruction as an opportunity to rebuild their corners of U.S. science — or even reimagine it, says Michael Osterholm, an epidemiologist at the University of Minnesota in Minneapolis. “If there’s any good that can come out of what has been a horrible situation, it’s that it’s given us time and provided a pause to think through clearly: Is this the way we want to continue?”
paras.zh: 然而，明尼阿波利斯明尼苏达大学的流行病学家迈克尔·奥斯特霍尔姆表示，一些研究人员将这次破坏视为重建美国科学角落的机会，甚至重新构想它。 “如果说可怕的局势能带来什么好处的话，那就是它给了我们时间，让我们有时间停下来清楚地思考：这是我们想要继续的方式吗？”

paras.en: University of Ottawa ecologist Julien Martin spent a decade building a respected lab that probed how social behaviors affect the evolution of bushy-tailed, cat-sized rodents called marmots. So when the National Science Foundation began its sweeping grant cuts, Martin found himself doing something unexpected: uploading cute marmot videos to OnlyFans, an online video subscription platform better known for hosting pornography.
paras.zh: 渥太华大学生态学家朱利安·马丁花了十年时间建立了一个受人尊敬的实验室，该实验室研究社会行为如何影响毛尾、猫大小的啮齿动物（土拨鼠）的进化。因此，当国家科学基金会开始大幅削减拨款时，马丁发现自己做了一些意想不到的事情：将可爱的土拨鼠视频上传到 OnlyFans，这是一个以托管色情内容而闻名的在线视频订阅平台。

paras.en: The effort, called OnlyMarms, netted $6,000 — a mere drop in the funding bucket. But the project went viral, leading outside supporters to launch a cryptocurrency token that earned the lab an additional $150,000. And direct donations, including an anonymous $300,000 gift, gave the lab enough to fund one Ph.D. student’s entire degree.
paras.zh: 这项名为 OnlyMarms 的项目筹集了 6,000 美元——这只是资金桶中的九牛一毛。但该项目迅速走红，导致外部支持者推出了加密货币代币，为实验室额外赚取了 15 万美元。直接捐赠，包括匿名的 30 万美元捐赠，为实验室提供了足够的资金资助一名博士生。学生的整个学位。

paras.en: “When you see that so much money could be obtained by doing essentially nothing about science, it’s quite shocking,” Martin says. He welcomes the support, but having to spend so much time on non-research tasks has also felt demeaning. “Sometimes, you have to question: Is the science funding broken? Are we just competing for pennies?”
paras.zh: “当你看到对科学基本上不做任何事情就能获得这么多钱时，这是相当令人震惊的，”马丁说。他对这种支持表示欢迎，但不得不在非研究任务上花费如此多的时间也让他感到有失尊严。 “有时候，你不得不问：科学资助是否被打破？我们只是为了几分钱而竞争吗？”

paras.en: In 2025, the National Institutes of Health and the NSF canceled or suspended more than 7,800 existing grants, totaling billions of dollars. (Some 5,200 grants were later reinstated.) Each agency issued roughly a quarter fewer grants in 2025 than their previous 10-year averages.
paras.zh: 2025 年，美国国立卫生研究院和美国国家科学基金会取消或暂停了 7,800 多项现有拨款，总额达数十亿美元。 （后来恢复了约 5,200 项拨款。）每个机构在 2025 年发放的拨款比之前 10 年平均水平大约减少四分之一。

paras.en: Universities and research centers were hit hard. “It was really dire,” says Emily Young, who leads medical research grantmaking at the San Diego-based Prebys Foundation. In phone calls with researchers, many told her they had halted ongoing experiments, such as developing measles vaccines for people with autoimmune disorders.
paras.zh: 大学和研究中心受到重创。 “这真的很可怕，”圣地亚哥普雷比斯基金会医学研究资助负责人艾米丽·杨 (Emily Young) 说。在与研究人员的电话中，许多人告诉她，他们已经停止了正在进行的实验，例如为患有自身免疫性疾病的人开发麻疹疫苗。

paras.en: But the thing that really stood out, Young says, was how the sudden drop in funding was affecting postdocs and early-career researchers. “Young people were going from feeling like they had an avenue for a really promising career … to feeling like they were in a worthless career.”
paras.zh: 但杨说，真正引人注目的是资金的突然减少对博士后和早期职业研究人员的影响。 “年轻人从感觉自己有一条通往真正有前途的职业的道路……到感觉自己的职业毫无价值。”

paras.en: So, in May 2025, the foundation awarded $7 million total in emergency grants to seven local institutions, including San Diego State University, the University of California, San Diego and Scripps Research. The grants targeted more than 80 research programs involving early- and mid-career scientists that were facing hundreds of millions of dollars in lost federal funding.
paras.zh: 因此，2025 年 5 月，该基金会向圣地亚哥州立大学、加州大学圣地亚哥分校和斯克里普斯研究中心等 7 个当地机构提供了总计 700 万美元的紧急赠款。这些赠款针对了 80 多个研究项目，涉及职业生涯早期和中期的科学家，这些项目面临着数亿美元的联邦资金损失。

paras.en: Larger science philanthropies also stepped into the breach. The Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation gave $55 million total to 30 universities to support 400 postdoctoral researchers. The Alfred P. Sloan and Spencer foundations, among others, partnered to provide 83 quick-turnaround grants of around $25,000 each to researchers whose NSF education grants had been canceled.
paras.zh: 更大的科学慈善机构也介入了这一缺口。戈登和贝蒂摩尔基金会向 30 所大学总共捐赠了 5500 万美元，用于支持 400 名博士后研究人员。 Alfred P. Sloan 和 Spencer 基金会等合作，向 NSF 教育补助金被取消的研究人员提供了 83 笔快速周转补助金，每人约 25,000 美元。

paras.en: Some wealthy universities also offered bridge funding to their researchers; Johns Hopkins University gave awards up to $250,000 to individuals with unexpected funding gaps, and the Yale School of Medicine arranged to fund up to 90 percent of terminated or frozen NIH grants.
paras.zh: 一些富裕的大学还为其研究人员提供过桥资助；约翰·霍普金斯大学向出现意外资金缺口的个人提供了高达 25 万美元的奖励，耶鲁大学医学院则安排为 90% 的终止或冻结的 NIH 拨款提供资金。

paras.en: After the first bout of funding chaos, science philanthropy Schmidt Sciences announced a more ambitious approach: to develop the science themselves. In January 2026, they revealed plans to construct three ground-based observatories and a space telescope larger than NASA’s Hubble by the end of the decade. The space telescope alone will cost hundreds of millions of dollars and provide open-access data to scientists worldwide, with a special focus on exoplanets and transient events like supernovas.
paras.zh: 在第一轮资金混乱之后，科学慈善机构施密特科学公司宣布了一个更加雄心勃勃的方法：自行发展科学。 2026 年 1 月，他们透露了计划在本世纪末建造三个地面观测站和一个比 NASA 哈勃望远镜还要大的太空望远镜。仅太空望远镜就将耗资数亿美元，并向全世界科学家提供开放获取的数据，特别关注系外行星和超新星等瞬态事件。

paras.en: In November 2026, the philanthropy opened its first round of funding for early-career scientists using the observatory system; individual awards will total up to $2.5 million each.
paras.zh: 2026 年 11 月，该慈善机构为使用天文台系统的早期职业科学家启动了第一轮资助；每项个人奖金总额最高可达 250 万美元。

paras.en: “Originally, the hope was we would play a more classic philanthropic role,” says Arpita Roy, an astronomer who directs the Astrophysics & Space Center at Schmidt Sciences. But given the federal funding landscape, she says, “it became pretty clear to us, if we really think these things need to exist in the world … then we need to build them out.”
paras.zh: “最初，我们希望能够扮演一个更经典的慈善角色，”施密特科学公司天体物理与太空中心的天文学家阿皮塔·罗伊 (Arpita Roy) 说。但考虑到联邦资金的情况，她说，“我们很清楚，如果我们真的认为这些东西需要存在于世界上……那么我们就需要建造它们。”

paras.en: While private funding can be a lifeline, Young says, it’s still a temporary measure at best. “We are not going to fill the vacuum of federal funding,” she says. “There is simply not enough philanthropic resource out there to do that.”
paras.zh: 杨说，虽然私人资金可以成为生命线，但它充其量也只是一种临时措施。 “我们不会填补联邦资金的真空，”她说。 “根本没有足够的慈善资源来做到这一点。”

paras.en: In 1995, the American Academy of Pediatrics and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention made a consequential decision: Rather than publish independent recommendations for childhood vaccines, as they had since the 1960s, they would issue one set jointly. Over the next 30 years, a group called the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices advised the CDC, with academy input, to expand its recommendations to include chickenpox, hepatitis A and pneumococcal infections. Cases of the three dropped by more than 90 percent, saving thousands of lives.
paras.zh: 1995 年，美国儿科学会和疾病控制与预防中心做出了一项重大决定：他们不再像 20 世纪 60 年代以来那样发布针对儿童疫苗的独立建议，而是联合发布一套。在接下来的 30 年里，一个名为免疫实践咨询委员会的组织建议 CDC 在学术界的投入下扩大其建议范围，将水痘、甲型肝炎和肺炎球菌感染包括在内。这三人的病例下降了 90% 以上，挽救了数千人的生命。

paras.en: But in June 2025, Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy Jr., an outspoken vaccine critic, fired all 17 members of ACIP and replaced many with vaccine skeptics. Kennedy also dismissed the academy representatives that informed the group.
paras.zh: 但在 2025 年 6 月，直言不讳的疫苗批评者、卫生与公众服务部部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪解雇了 ACIP 的全部 17 名成员，并用疫苗怀疑论者取代了许多成员。肯尼迪还解雇了向该组织通报情况的学院代表。

paras.en: “Essentially, we had no voice anymore,” recalls O’Leary, the pediatric infectious disease researcher at the University of Colorado Anschutz. He also serves as the AAP’s immunization schedule editor. “So we made a decision to not participate until we could say, ‘OK, this is a body that can be trusted.’ ”
paras.zh: “从本质上讲，我们不再有发言权了，”科罗拉多大学安舒茨分校的儿科传染病研究员奥利里回忆道。他还担任 AAP 的免疫接种计划编辑。 “所以我们决定不参加，直到我们可以说，‘好吧，这是一个可以信任的机构。’”

paras.en: In July 2025, the academy and other public health groups sued over the ACIP firings. The committee was unable to meet due to the lawsuit, and over the next six months, the CDC removed recommendations from its childhood vaccination schedule including hepatitis A and B, COVID-19 and meningococcal disease. The American Academy of Pediatrics issued its own schedule including those vaccines in January 2026.
paras.zh: 2025 年 7 月，学院和其他公共卫生组织就 ACIP 解雇事件提起诉讼。由于诉讼，该委员会无法召开会议，在接下来的六个月里，疾病预防控制中心从其儿童疫苗接种计划中删除了建议，包括甲型和乙型肝炎、COVID-19 和脑膜炎球菌病。美国儿科学会于 2026 年 1 月发布了自己的时间表，其中包括这些疫苗。

paras.en: The loss of trustworthy federal recommendations leaves “an impossible gap to fill,” O’Leary says. But when it came to stepping in, “from my perspective, there was not an alternative.” The academy has since collaborated with the Vaccine Integrity Project, a new group led by Osterholm, to conduct the scientific reviews that inform vaccine recommendations.
paras.zh: 奥利里说，失去值得信赖的联邦建议留下了“一个无法填补的空白”。但当谈到介入时，“从我的角度来看，没有其他选择。”此后，该学院与奥斯特霍尔姆领导的新组织疫苗完整性项目合作，进行科学审查，为疫苗建议提供信息。

paras.en: Vaccines weren’t the only childhood health matter to get a shakeup. In April 2025, HHS terminated the Advisory Committee on Heritable Disorders in Newborns and Children, which formulates newborn screening recommendations for genetic disorders, many of which can be deadly or disabling. Currently, some 98 percent of U.S.-born infants are screened at birth.
paras.zh: 疫苗并不是唯一一个需要改变的儿童健康问题。 2025 年 4 月，HHS 终止了新生儿和儿童遗传性疾病咨询委员会，该委员会负责制定针对遗传性疾病的新生儿筛查建议，其中许多遗传性疾病可能是致命的或致残的。目前，约 98% 的美国出生婴儿在出生时接受了筛查。

paras.en: When the genetics community raised concerns, Cynthia Powell, a retired pediatric geneticist at the University of North Carolina School of Medicine in Chapel Hill, gathered around 15 representatives of professional medical societies to create the Newborn Screening Collaborative. With support from the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics, the group began meeting in early 2026.
paras.zh: 当遗传学界提出担忧时，北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校医学院的退休儿科遗传学家 Cynthia Powell 召集了大约 15 名专业医学会的代表，创建了新生儿筛查合作组织。在美国医学遗传学和基因组学学院的支持下，该小组于 2026 年初开始召开会议。

paras.en: While the collaborative cannot give direct recommendations to HHS, it hopes to conduct evidence reviews for states and the small, parent-led advocacy groups that form around rare diseases, Powell says. It plans to focus on conditions that already have treatments under development, like a rare metabolic disorder known as Sanfilippo syndrome type A.
paras.zh: 鲍威尔说，虽然该合作组织无法向美国卫生与公众服务部提供直接建议，但它希望为各州以及围绕罕见疾病组成的小型、由家长领导的倡导团体进行证据审查。它计划重点关注已经有正在开发的治疗方法的疾病，例如一种被称为 A 型 Sanfilippo 综合征的罕见代谢性疾病。

paras.en: Approximate number of NIH and NSF grants canceled or suspended in 2025. Some 5,200 have since been reinstated
paras.zh: 2025 年取消或暂停的 NIH 和 NSF 拨款的大约数量。此后约有 5,200 项拨款已恢复

paras.en: “This Newborn Screening Collaborative is another effort not to leave a complete void,” says Jewel Mullen, an epidemiologist at the University of Texas at Austin who was lead editor on a May 2025 newborn screening report for the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine.
paras.zh: 德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校的流行病学家 Jewel Mullen 说：“这个新生儿筛查合作组织是为了不留下完全空白而做出的另一项努力。”他是美国国家科学、工程和医学院 2025 年 5 月新生儿筛查报告的主编。

paras.en: Other researchers are filling gaps in awareness about public health threats. A philanthropy-backed group called the Evidence Collective posted about the diarrhea-causing cyclosporiasis outbreak before the CDC’s Health Alert Network did. The collective, made up of more than 30 medical communicators, has more than 10 million followers across social media and notched 11 billion impressions in 2025.
paras.zh: 其他研究人员正在填补人们对公共卫生威胁的认识空白。一个名为 Evidence Collective 的慈善组织在疾病预防控制中心的健康警报网络发布之前发布了有关导致腹泻的环孢子虫病爆发的信息。该团体由 30 多名医疗传播者组成，在社交媒体上拥有超过 1000 万粉丝，到 2025 年曝光量将达到 110 亿次。

paras.en: “I don’t think that we will ever be able to fully replace the infrastructure that was there through the federal government,” says Madison, a founding member of the collective. But “there is a concerted effort now to look at: How do we take the momentum that we have with these organizations, and then make it sustainable?”
paras.zh: “我认为我们永远无法完全取代联邦政府现有的基础设施，”该集体的创始成员麦迪逊说。但“现在需要共同努力：我们如何利用与这些组织的合作势头，然后使其可持续发展？”

paras.en: Although stopgap measures are succeeding so far, scientists see them as Band-Aids at best. “We’re going to do it for as long as we’re needed,” Osterholm says. But “I look forward to the day when we’re not going to be needed anymore.”
paras.zh: 尽管权宜之计到目前为止取得了成功，但科学家们认为它们充其量只是创可贴。 “只要需要，我们就会这样做，”奥斯特霍尔姆说。但“我期待着有一天不再需要我们。”

paras.en: In April 2025, nearly 400 scientists working on the National Climate Assessment, a recurring, congressionally mandated report, received an email that it was being reevaluated and they were being released from their work. One of them — Rutgers University climate scientist Bob Kopp — wasn’t surprised. “I don’t think you have to speculate very far” to know why, Kopp says. He cites a directive in the White House’s 2027 budget request to “stop wasting biological and environmental research resources on climate change.”
paras.zh: 2025 年 4 月，近 400 名从事国家气候评估（国会授权的定期报告）工作的科学家收到一封电子邮件，称该报告正在重新评估，他们的工作将被解除。其中一位——罗格斯大学气候科学家鲍勃·科普——对此并不感到惊讶。科普说，“我认为你不必进行太多推测”就能知道原因。他引用了白宫 2027 年预算请求中的一项指令，即“停止在气候变化问题上浪费生物和环境研究资源”。

paras.en: However, “there was an immediate and deep sentiment by the science community to continue the work,” says environmental engineer Costa Samaras of Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh, who had also been involved with the climate report. He and colleagues asked the American Geophysical Union and the American Meteorological Society to help organize the U.S. Climate Collection, a new set of papers from scientists about climate research, risks and solutions that will keep the public informed until federal assessments resume.
paras.zh: 然而，“科学界立即强烈地希望继续这项工作，”匹兹堡卡内基梅隆大学的环境工程师科斯塔·萨马拉斯说，他也参与了气候报告的编写。他和同事请求美国地球物理联盟和美国气象学会帮助组织美国气候收集，这是一组由科学家撰写的关于气候研究、风险和解决方案的新论文，将在联邦评估恢复之前向公众通报情况。

paras.en: While the work is promising, “a volunteer effort of 170 scientists cannot substitute for a $30 million effort of 600 people,” Kopp says.
paras.zh: 尽管这项工作前景广阔，但“170 名科学家的志愿者努力无法替代 600 人花费 3000 万美元的努力，”Kopp 说。

paras.en: The American Geophysical Union similarly stepped in with crucial financing for the Arctic Report Card, an annual report from NOAA that has provided information about the changing Arctic since 2006. Its editors were blindsided when they found out during a routine meeting in August 2026 that NOAA was withdrawing its support.
paras.zh: 美国地球物理联盟同样介入，为《北极报告卡》提供了重要资金，这是 NOAA 的一份年度报告，提供了自 2006 年以来有关北极变化的信息。当其编辑在 2026 年 8 月的例行会议上发现 NOAA 正在撤回其支持时，他们大吃一惊。

paras.en: AGU’s in-kind offer to support the project just one month later was “tremendous,” says Twila Moon, a glaciologist at the National Snow and Ice Data Center in Boulder, Colo., who edits the report card. “But [it] is not a kind of model that is sustainable into the future.”
paras.zh: 科罗拉多州博尔德国家冰雪数据中心的冰川学家、负责编辑报告单的特威拉·穆恩 (Twila Moon) 表示，仅仅一个月后，AGU 就为该项目提供了“巨大的实物支持”。 “但[它]并不是一种可以持续到未来的模式。”

paras.en: AGU President Brandon Jones agrees. Nevertheless, at the time, the organization “had this sense of what was moral, what was right, what was ethical,” Jones says. And given AGU’s resources, “it seemed like it was our turn to show up and step up and act like the union that we’ve always been.”
paras.zh: AGU 主席布兰登·琼斯对此表示同意。尽管如此，琼斯说，当时该组织“对什么是道德、什么是正确、什么是道德有这种感觉”。考虑到 AGU 的资源，“看来现在轮到我们站出来，像我们一直以来的工会一样行事了。”

paras.en: The Planetary Society, a nonprofit space advocacy organization based in Pasadena, Calif., took the lead on several committees that NASA dropped. In January, the agency cited executive orders as it withdrew financial and logistical support from eight groups of space scientists and experts that advised NASA’s planning teams on exploring asteroids, comets and planets.
paras.zh: 行星协会是一个总部位于加利福尼亚州帕萨迪纳的非营利性太空倡导组织，在美国宇航局放弃的几个委员会中发挥了带头作用。一月份，该机构援引行政命令，撤回了八组空间科学家和专家的财务和后勤支持，这些专家组为 NASA 规划团队探索小行星、彗星和行星提供建议。

paras.en: “It was pretty well-managed and organized [before], and then really fell apart because of the intrusion of the executive orders,” says Jack Kiraly, chief of advocacy at the Planetary Society. The organization now hosts the advisory groups’ websites, documents and meetings. “We’ve basically been having to reinvent this whole system.”
paras.zh: 行星协会的宣传主管杰克·基拉利（Jack Kiraly）表示：“（之前）管理和组织得相当好，但后来由于行政命令的介入而真正崩溃了。”该组织现在托管咨询小组的网站、文件和会议。 “我们基本上不得不重新发明整个系统。”

paras.en: Climate.us isn’t the only site saving federal data. In November 2024, many environmental organizations “started preparing for the worst,” says Brittany Janis, executive director of the Open Environmental Data Project. Her group and nine others banded together to create the Public Environmental Data Partners, a network of 400 volunteers that archive environmental data and tools they suspected “would probably be on the chopping block.”
paras.zh: Climate.us 并不是唯一保存联邦数据的网站。开放环境数据项目执行董事布列塔尼·贾尼斯 (Brittany Janis) 表示，2024 年 11 月，许多环保组织“开始为最坏的情况做准备”。她的团队和其他九个人联合起来创建了公共环境数据合作伙伴，这是一个由 400 名志愿者组成的网络，负责归档他们怀疑“可能会被砍掉”的环境数据和工具。

paras.en: In February 2025, the Environmental Protection Agency deleted a tool called EJScreen, which maps places where people face high levels of risk from environmental burdens such as hazardous waste and ozone. Within 48 hours, the partnership had stood up EJScreen on a new website, using open-source files to reverse engineer and refine the data pipelines. It has since received 1,000 views a month, Janis says.
paras.zh: 2025 年 2 月，环境保护局删除了一个名为 EJScreen 的工具，该工具绘制了人们面临危险废物和臭氧等环境负担高风险的地方。 48 小时内，合作伙伴就在新网站上建立了 EJScreen，使用开源文件进行逆向工程和完善数据管道。 Janis 说，此后每月有 1,000 次浏览。

paras.en: Nearly $2 million in philanthropic funding has helped the project pay staff, host data and hire engineers. It has restored the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s Future Risk Index, which projects county-level economic losses from climate change; the White House Council on Environmental Quality’s Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool, which identifies communities overburdened by pollution; and the Department of Homeland Security’s Homeland Infrastructure Foundation-Level Data tool, which maps infrastructure at risk of natural disasters.
paras.zh: 近 200 万美元的慈善资金帮助该项目支付员工工资、托管数据和雇用工程师。它恢复了联邦紧急事务管理局的未来风险指数，该指数预测了气候变化造成的县级经济损失；白宫环境质量委员会的气候和经济正义筛查工具，该工具可识别污染负担过重的社区；国土安全部的国土基础设施基础级数据工具，用于绘制面临自然灾害风险的基础设施地图。

paras.en: “We should not misunderstand the administration’s closing off of this data [to mean] that they don’t think data is important,” Janis says. “They recognize how important it is — and how valuable it is to causes that they disagree with.”
paras.zh: “我们不应该误解政府关闭这些数据[意味着]他们认为数据不重要，”贾尼斯说。 “他们认识到它的重要性，以及它对于他们不同意的事业的价值。”

paras.en: At the University of Chicago, the Data Mirror Project preserves datasets larger than one terabyte, including those from the U.S. Census Bureau and the National Park Service. The project has a guiding principle: LOCKSS, which stands for lots of copies keeps stuff safe, says colead Lisa Chinn, who is head of research data services at the university library. An agency doesn’t have to delete its data to create problems, she adds. Firing website staff can lead to wonky links, corrupted files and pages that degrade into Wingdings gibberish.
paras.zh: 在芝加哥大学，数据镜像项目保存了超过 1 TB 的数据集，包括来自美国人口普查局和国家公园管理局的数据集。该项目有一个指导原则：LOCKSS，代表大量副本，保证资料安全，该大学图书馆研究数据服务主管、共同负责人丽莎·钦 (Lisa Chinn) 说。她补充说，机构不必删除其数据来制造问题。解雇网站员工可能会导致链接不稳定、文件损坏以及页面退化为 Wingdings 乱码。

paras.en: The thought of losing all that data can be stressful, Janis says, but “there’s a lot of parachutes that have gone out.”
paras.zh: 贾尼斯说，一想到丢失所有数据就会感到压力很大，但“有很多降落伞已经失效了。”

paras.en: Even as researchers, volunteers and scientific organizations pick up the pieces of the federal science enterprise, some are already imagining new ways of shaping it. “The world was not perfect in 2024,” says Rutgers’ Kopp. “Reconstruction is an opportunity to improve upon the way things are done.”
paras.zh: 尽管研究人员、志愿者和科学组织正在收拾联邦科学事业的碎片，但有些人已经在想象塑造它的新方法。 “2024 年的世界并不完美，”罗格斯大学的科普说。 “重建是改进工作方式的机会。”

paras.en: To Mullen, the epidemiologist at the University of Texas at Austin, transparency is key. New bodies like the Vaccine Integrity Project and the Newborn Screening Collaborative should make their meetings and deliberations as open as possible, she says, especially when “people think that those with the loudest voices or the biggest wallets are going to be the ones that have the greatest influence behind the scenes.”
paras.zh: 对于德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校的流行病学家马伦来说，透明度是关键。她说，像疫苗完整性项目和新生儿筛查合作组织这样的新机构应该让他们的会议和审议尽可能公开，尤其是当“人们认为那些声音最大或财力最大的人将是在幕后影响力最大的人”时。

paras.en: Powell, of the Newborn Screening Collaborative, is hoping for greater efficiency in the disease recommendation process. Previously, it could take as long as three years to bring a condition from an initial vote to a final recommendation; with the collaborative, she hopes it could take one to three months.
paras.zh: 新生儿筛查合作组织的鲍威尔希望提高疾病推荐过程的效率。此前，一项条件从最初投票到最终建议可能需要长达三年的时间；通过合作，她希望能够花费一到三个月的时间。

paras.en: Janis, of the Open Environmental Data Project, hopes to develop more creative and flexible data tools for researchers based on their needs. And Madison from the Evidence Collective and Martin of OnlyMarms believe that the science infrastructure needs to diversify its funding sources to prevent future shocks.
paras.zh: 开放环境数据项目的Janis希望根据研究人员的需求，为他们开发更具创意、更灵活的数据工具。 Evidence Collective 的麦迪逊和 OnlyMarms 的马丁认为，科学基础设施需要使其资金来源多样化，以防止未来的冲击。

paras.en: However, Janis notes that there are inherent risks in having the private sector support public goods such as open information. And Kopp warns that “attempts to replace something that was well-functioning … are not going to necessarily end up with something that is better or even as good as what was there before.”
paras.zh: 然而，贾尼斯指出，让私营部门支持开放信息等公共产品存在固有的风险。科普警告说，“尝试取代运行良好的东西……最终不一定会得到比以前更好甚至一样好的东西。”

paras.en: At the end of the day, one of the key elements in establishing a new science system is “faith that you will still exist in a year or 10 years or maybe even 20 years,” says Katharine Jacobs, an environmental scientist who directed a previous National Climate Assessment under President Obama. Without stable institutional funding, “we are all essentially wasting our time, bashing our heads against the wall, trying to create a system that we can’t support,” Jacobs says.
paras.zh: 归根结底，建立新科学体系的关键要素之一是“相信一年、十年甚至二十年后你仍然会存在”，曾指导奥巴马总统领导下的国家气候评估的环境科学家凯瑟琳·雅各布斯 (Katharine Jacobs) 说。雅各布斯说，如果没有稳定的机构资金，“我们基本上都是在浪费时间，把头撞在墙上，试图创建一个我们无法支持的体系。”

paras.en: For the Lindsey sisters, being involved in public service — even outside the government aegis — has been empowering, especially during what they see as an otherwise dark period for science.
paras.zh: 对于林赛姐妹来说，参与公共服务——即使是在政府支持之外——一直是一种赋权，尤其是在她们认为科学的黑暗时期。

paras.en: They have raised more than $600,000 from individual donations since August 2025. And in February, they received a one-time grant from the Doris Duke Foundation and others that will cover their salaries and benefits until February 2027.
paras.zh: 自 2025 年 8 月以来，他们已通过个人捐款筹集了超过 60 万美元。今年 2 月，他们收到了 Doris Duke 基金会和其他机构的一次性赠款，该赠款将支付他们直到 2027 年 2 月的工资和福利。

paras.en: “If we can get the money, I can see us doing this indefinitely,” Rebecca Lindsey says. She still hopes to retire one day, and she fights off worries that the government might come knocking about their unsanctioned work. But “we had a public that trusted us,” she says about jumping into the fray. “It was a risk worth taking.”
paras.zh: “如果我们能拿到钱，我可以看到我们无限期地这样做，”丽贝卡·林赛说。她仍然希望有一天能退休，并消除了政府可能会批评他们未经批准的工作的担忧。但“我们有一群信任我们的公众，”她在谈到加入这场争论时说道。 “这是一个值得冒的风险。”

articles.title: U.S. demand for menopause hormone therapy has more than doubled recently
articles.author: Aimee Cunningham

paras.en: More U.S. women are taking menopause hormone therapy, new prescription data suggest.
paras.zh: 新的处方数据显示，越来越多的美国女性正在接受更年期激素疗法。

paras.en: Monthly dispensing of hormone therapy for women aged 40 to 74 more than doubled since 2023, growing from 2 million to 4.9 million, researchers report November 19 in JAMA. The analysis of U.S. pharmacy dispensing data revealed that this increase began in 2024. The rise continued in 2025, before and after the Food and Drug Administration’s November removal of the black box warning from packaging, and into 2026.
paras.zh: 研究人员 11 月 19 日在《美国医学会杂志》上报告称，自 2023 年以来，每月为 40 至 74 岁女性发放激素治疗的人数增加了一倍多，从 200 万增加到 490 万。对美国药房配药数据的分析显示，这种增长始于 2024 年。这种增长持续到 2025 年，即食品和药物管理局 11 月从包装上去除黑框警告之前和之后，一直持续到 2026 年。

paras.en: Although the data in the new study are aggregate, the researchers used population data to estimate the dispensing rate for this age group, which jumped from 28 prescriptions per 1,000 women to 67 prescriptions per 1,000 over the period studied.
paras.zh: 尽管新研究中的数据是汇总的，但研究人员使用人口数据来估计该年龄组的配药率，在研究期间，配药率从每 1,000 名女性 28 处方跃升至每 1,000 名女性 67 处方。

paras.en: The new study wasn’t designed to determine what’s behind the increase. It’s possible that the evidence regarding hormone therapy’s safety and effectiveness for the treatment of menopause symptoms, such as hot flashes, is reaching more women. Medical groups such as the Menopause Society have recommended menopause hormone therapy for women with symptoms who are younger than 60 or within 10 years of the start of menopause, absent certain risk factors including prior breast cancer and stroke.
paras.zh: 这项新研究的目的并不是为了确定这一增长背后的原因。有关激素疗法治疗潮热等更年期症状的安全性和有效性的证据可能正在惠及更多女性。更年期协会等医疗团体建议年龄小于 60 岁或绝经开始后 10 年内有症状的女性接受更年期激素治疗，且不存在某些危险因素，包括既往乳腺癌和中风。

paras.en: “Greater attention to women’s health, updated medical guidance supporting individualized menopause hormone therapy and social media may all be contributing to increased interest,” says Dana Sarnak, who studies sexual and reproductive health at Johns Hopkins School of Medicine. Anecdotally, her clinician colleagues report more patients seeking menopause care, she says.
paras.zh: “对女性健康的更多关注、支持个体化更年期激素治疗的最新医疗指南和社交媒体都可能有助于增加人们的兴趣，”约翰·霍普金斯大学医学院研究性健康和生殖健康的达纳·萨纳克 (Dana Sarnak) 说。她说，有趣的是，她的临床医生同事报告说，越来越多的患者寻求更年期护理。

paras.en: Many women and physicians turned away from hormone therapy in the early 2000s after a large study called the Women’s Health Initiative raised safety concerns, which were later considered overblown. Research since then has provided a more nuanced understanding of the benefits and risks of menopause hormone therapy at different ages.
paras.zh: 2000 年代初，一项名为“女性健康倡议”的大型研究提出了安全问题，之后许多女性和医生放弃了激素治疗，但后来认为该研究有些夸大其词。此后的研究对不同年龄的更年期激素治疗的益处和风险提供了更细致的了解。

paras.en: There are safer formulations, including patches and gels, of estrogen today then at the time of the Women’s Health Initiative, for which participants took a pill. The new study found that product use increased for transdermal and vaginal estrogen and for progesterone products — women who have their uterus need to take progesterone along with estrogen. The use of oral formulations remained stable. There has been a shortage of estrogen patches in the United States this year, which the U.S. Food and Drug Administration attributes to increasing demand.
paras.zh: 现在有更安全的雌激素配方，包括贴剂和凝胶，而在妇女健康倡议时期，参与者服用的是药丸。这项新研究发现，透皮和阴道雌激素以及黄体酮产品的使用量有所增加——有子宫的女性需要在服用雌激素的同时服用黄体酮。口服制剂的使用保持稳定。今年美国出现雌激素贴剂短缺的情况，美国食品和药物管理局将其归因于需求增加。

articles.title: A brain region known for listening helps us speak
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: WASHINGTON — A part of the brain famous for listening is important for talking, too.
paras.zh: 华盛顿——大脑中以倾听闻名的部分对于说话也很重要。

paras.en: Data collected from people as they listen and try to talk show that this brain region, a small spot inside a larger area called Wernicke’s area, has a more expansive job than researchers thought when it comes to communicating. The results may help efforts to restore people’s voices. The results presented November 15 at the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience and published November 19 in Science.
paras.zh: 从人们倾听和尝试说话时收集的数据表明，这个大脑区域是一个名为韦尼克区的较大区域内的一个小点，在交流方面比研究人员想象的更广泛。研究结果可能有助于恢复人们的声音。研究结果于 11 月 15 日在神经科学学会年会上公布，并于 11 月 19 日发表在《科学》杂志上。

paras.en: The study provides convincing evidence that this brain spot is critical for speech production, says neurologist and language researcher Jeffrey Binder of the Medical College of Wisconsin in Milwaukee. “My hope is that this study will help scientists and clinicians accept a more accurate interpretation of this focal area” as an early stop on the pathway to saying a word.
paras.zh: 密尔沃基威斯康星医学院的神经学家和语言研究员杰弗里·宾德说，这项研究提供了令人信服的证据，证明这个大脑斑点对于言语产生至关重要。 “我希望这项研究能够帮助科学家和临床医生接受对这个重点领域的更准确的解释”，作为说话之路的早期终点。

paras.en: A small part of the brain, just above the left ear, was first described in 1874 by a neurologist Carl Wernicke as necessary for making sense of speech. People with damage there had trouble comprehending words. But some people also had trouble producing them. “Sounds were swapped, words were replaced with near misses,” Edward Chang of the University of California, San Francisco, said in a news briefing. “The basic question has been, ‘Why would damage to a hearing area of the brain break the ability to speak?’ That question has been open for 150 years.”
paras.zh: 1874 年，神经学家卡尔·韦尼克 (Carl Wernicke) 首次将大脑左耳上方的一小部分描述为理解言语所必需的部分。那里受到伤害的人无法理解言语。但有些人在生产它们时也遇到了困难。加州大学旧金山分校的爱德华·张（Edward Chang）在新闻发布会上表示：“声音被调换了，语言也被差点儿取代了。” “基本问题是，‘为什么大脑听力区域受损会导致说话能力丧失？’这个问题已经存在了 150 年。”

paras.en: The new research offers an answer: A small bit of Wernicke’s area (to be extremely specific, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus or lpSTG ) becomes active just before a word is spoken. “Every word that you have said today began in that small part above your left ear about a quarter of a second before you said it,” Chang said.
paras.zh: 这项新研究提供了答案：韦尼克区的一小部分（非常具体地说，是左后颞上回或 lpSTG）在说出单词之前变得活跃。 “你今天所说的每一个字都是在你说之前大约四分之一秒开始于你左耳上方的那个小部分的，”张说。

paras.en: The finding adds to growing evidence that brain areas are more complex than people have appreciated, says neuroscientist Leigh Hochberg at Brown University in Providence, R.I. “I believe that one of the things we are going to learn over the next five, 10 years of this research, is that each part of the brain that, we were taught as a med student or a grad student, does this, probably does that and a whole lot more.”
paras.zh: 罗德岛州普罗维登斯布朗大学的神经科学家 Leigh Hochberg 表示，这一发现进一步证明大脑区域比人们想象的更为复杂。“我相信，在接下来的五年、十年的研究中，我们将了解到的一件事是，我们作为医学生或研究生所学到的大脑的每个部分都可以做这个，也可能做那个，甚至更多。”

paras.en: Scientists measured brain activity in 28 people before they had surgery for epilepsy or tumors. They were able to see that this brain region kicked on as a person listened to words, and also just before they attempted to speak. Cells there had preferences for certain sorts of words, long ones, for instance. “It’s more active when you’re about to say the word caterpillar than when you’re about to say the word cat,” said Matthew Leonard, a cognitive neuroscientist at UCSF.
paras.zh: 科学家测量了 28 名接受癫痫或肿瘤手术的人的大脑活动。他们能够看到，当一个人听单词时，以及在他们试图说话之前，这个大脑区域就会启动。那里的细胞对某些类型的单词有偏好，例如长单词。加州大学旧金山分校的认知神经科学家马修·伦纳德 (Matthew Leonard) 表示：“当你要说‘毛毛虫’这个词时，它比当你要说‘猫’这个词时更活跃。”

paras.en: Electrical stimulation to this small bit of brain also interfered with people’s ability to talk. “What we found was that stimulation, really only in this lpSTG area, disrupted this speech production when it was delivered just prior to speaking,” said UCSF bioengineer Alexander Silva.
paras.zh: 对这一小块大脑的电刺激也会干扰人们的说话能力。加州大学旧金山分校生物工程师亚历山大·席尔瓦 (Alexander Silva) 表示：“我们发现，只有在 lpSTG 区域的刺激才会在说话之前扰乱这种言语的产生。”

paras.en: Some efforts to make implanted devices that can help restore speech to people who no longer talk focus on the motor cortex, a part of the brain that controls the movements required for speech. This bit of Wernicke’s area offers an additional spot to consider, Silva said. “What if you could target a single brain region and gain access to the full spectrum of speech, from listening all the way up to speech production?”
paras.zh: 一些制造植入设备的努力可以帮助不再说话的人恢复言语，这些努力集中在运动皮层上，运动皮层是大脑中控制言语所需运动的部分。席尔瓦说，韦尼克的这一区域提供了另一个值得考虑的地方。 “如果你可以针对单个大脑区域并获得从聆听到言语产生的全部语音范围，会怎么样？”

paras.en: Experimental brain implants in two volunteers with paralysis were able to detect both what they heard and what they were trying to say, the researchers report in the study.
paras.zh: 研究人员在研究中报告说，两名瘫痪志愿者的实验性大脑植入物能够检测到他们听到的内容和他们想说的话。

paras.en: The discovery may help scientists better understand situations that involve both hearing and speaking, such as speech or comprehension differences in people with autism, or how children first begin learning to talk, Chang said.
paras.zh: 张说，这一发现可能有助于科学家更好地了解涉及听力和口语的情况，例如自闭症患者的言语或理解差异，或者儿童如何开始学习说话。

articles.title: Scientists Find a Strange 405,000-Year Pattern in Earth's Ancient Storms
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: There's a satisfying rhythm to life on this Earth.
paras.zh: 地球上的生命有一种令人满意的节奏。

paras.en: Day turns into night, and into day again. Spring rolls into summer, then fall, then winter, before flowers tentatively emerge from the thawing soil once more, while the Moon in the sky cycles from full to dark and back to full.
paras.zh: 白天变成黑夜，又变成白天。春天进入夏天，然后是秋天，然后是冬天，然后花朵再次从解冻的土壤中试探性地出现，而天空中的月亮则从满月到黑暗，再回到满月。

paras.en: But these are merely some of Earth's pulses, the ones we can measure in the spans of our own lives. The planet itself is vastly more ancient, and some of its cycles are longer than the entire history of humanity.
paras.zh: 但这些只是地球脉冲的一部分，我们可以在自己的一生中测量到这些脉冲。这个星球本身要古老得多，它的一些周期比整个人类历史还要长。

paras.en: And one, written in the geological record, may have a link to our planet's long, slow dance with the Sun.
paras.zh: 其中一项记录在地质记录中，可能与我们的星球与太阳的漫长而缓慢的舞蹈有关。

paras.en: In ancient layers of rock, deposits left by powerful storms appear to rise and fall in abundance on a cycle of roughly 405,000 years.
paras.zh: 在古老的岩层中，强大风暴留下的沉积物似乎以大约 405,000 年的周期大量升降。

paras.en: That pattern, according to a paper led by geologist Shuyuan Shi of China's Research Institute of Petroleum Exploration and Development, could be driven by periodic changes in Earth's orbit called Milankovitch cycles, as our planet is gently tugged by other planets in the Solar System.
paras.zh: 根据中国石油勘探开发研究院地质学家史书元领导的一篇论文，这种模式可能是由地球轨道的周期性变化（称为米兰科维奇周期）驱动的，因为我们的星球受到太阳系其他行星的轻轻牵引。

paras.en: This would mean that, instead of entirely random spates of increased activity, our planet's storms may have followed a surprisingly predictable ebb and flow.
paras.zh: 这意味着，我们星球的风暴可能不是完全随机地增加活动，而是遵循令人惊讶的可预测的潮起潮落。

paras.en: Storms are among the wildest weather events our atmosphere can create, including torrential rains and howling winds, a veritable frenzy of activity.
paras.zh: 风暴是我们的大气层可以造成的最狂野的天气事件之一，包括倾盆大雨和呼啸的狂风，这是一种名副其实的疯狂活动。

paras.en: You might think that this would scour the planet of all traces as it went, but all the material swept up in a storm has to go somewhere – and that somewhere can be the floor of the ocean.
paras.zh: 你可能会认为这会冲刷掉地球上所有的痕迹，但风暴中卷走的所有物质都必须去往某个地方——而那个地方可能是海底。

paras.en: Powerful waves and currents can churn up sand, silt, and mud from the seafloor, carry it away, and deposit it in new layers that are eventually buried beneath subsequent sediments.
