paras.en: If you repeatedly shuffle a deck of 10 playing cards using exactly the same method, what is the largest number of shuffles you could need before the deck returns to its original order?
paras.zh: 如果您使用完全相同的方法重复洗一副 10 张扑克牌，那么在这副牌恢复到原来的顺序之前，您最多需要洗多少次？

paras.en: For example, a silly shuffle might simply involve swapping the top and bottom cards, while leaving the rest untouched. After only two applications of this shuffle, the deck is restored. What about for more complicated shuffles? Note: shuffles are based only on the cards’ positions, not the specific card. For example, you can say, “Always move the top card down four positions,” but you cannot say, “Always move the queen of spades down four positions.”
paras.zh: 例如，愚蠢的洗牌可能只是交换顶部和底部的牌，而其余的则保持不变。仅进行两次洗牌后，牌组就恢复了。那么对于更复杂的洗牌呢？注意：洗牌仅基于纸牌的位置，而不是特定的纸牌。例如，您可以说“始终将顶牌向下移动四个位置”，但不能说“始终将黑桃皇后向下移动四个位置”。

paras.en: It will take a maximum of 30 shuffles before the deck returns to its original order.
paras.zh: 最多需要洗牌 30 次，牌组才会恢复到原来的顺序。

paras.en: Every shuffle, no matter how complicated, ultimately maps each position in the deck to another position, i.e., a shuffle is some permutation of the deck. Permutations can always be decomposed into discrete cycles. To understand this, consider the example shuffle given below, where the top card ends up in the sixth position, the second card moves to the top, etcetera.
paras.zh: 每次洗牌，无论多么复杂，最终都会将牌组中的每个位置映射到另一个位置，即洗牌是牌组的某种排列。排列总是可以分解为离散的循环。为了理解这一点，请考虑下面给出的洗牌示例，其中顶部的牌最终位于第六位置，第二张牌移动到顶部，等等。

paras.en: Follow the card that starts on top. The first shuffle moves it to position six, the second moves it from position six to position nine, the third to position two and the fourth back to position one. So it travels around a cycle of four positions: one → six → nine → two → one. Notice that the cards that begin in positions two, six and nine also travel along this same cycle before returning to their original positions. Following the other cards, you’ll find that this shuffle can be decomposed into cycles of lengths four, three, two and one. Every card belongs to some cycle, and no card belongs to two different cycles. (Every position points to one other position and is pointed to from one other position. To take part in two cycles, a position would have to point to two different places or be pointed to from two different places.)
paras.zh: 按照从顶部开始的卡片进行操作。第一次洗牌将其移至位置六，第二次将其从位置六移至位置九，第三次移至位置二，第四次移回位置一。因此它围绕四个位置循环：一→六→九→二→一。请注意，从位置 2、6 和 9 开始的卡片在返回到其原始位置之前也会沿着相同的循环移动。顺着其他牌看，你会发现这个洗牌可以分解为长度为四、三、二、一的循环。每张牌都属于某个周期，并且没有一张牌属于两个不同的周期。 （每个位置都指向另一个位置，并且从另一个位置指向。要参与两个循环，一个位置必须指向两个不同的位置或从两个不同的位置指向。）

paras.en: Every shuffle can be decomposed in this way. The length of a cycle represents the number of cards in that cycle, so the lengths always sum to 10. For example, the shuffle that simply takes the top card and puts it on the bottom would create one big cycle of length 10. The vacuous “shuffle” that declines to move any cards decomposes into 10 “cycles” each of length one.
paras.zh: 每个shuffle都可以这样分解。循环的长度代表该循环中纸牌的数量，因此长度之和始终为 10。例如，简单地取出顶部纸牌并将其放在底部的洗牌将创建一个长度为 10 的大循环。拒绝移动任何纸牌的空洞“洗牌”分解为 10 个“循环”，每个循环长度为 1。

paras.en: A card in a cycle of length three returns to its starting position after three shuffles and then again after six, nine, 12, and so on. So the whole deck is back in order the first time that every cycle has completed a whole number of trips around. That’s the least common multiple of the cycle lengths. To make the deck take as long as possible to return, we want to split 10 into cycle lengths with the largest possible least common multiple.
paras.zh: 长度为 3 的循环中的一张牌在洗牌三次后返回到其起始位置，然后在 6、9、12 等之后再次返回到其起始位置。因此，当每个周期完成了整数次循环时，整个甲板第一次恢复正常。这是周期长度的最小公倍数。为了使牌组返回的时间尽可能长，我们希望将 10 个循环长度分成尽可能大的最小公倍数。

paras.en: Cycles whose lengths share a common factor waste cards. Cycles of four and six, for example, are both back in place after 12 shuffles, but cycles of four and three are as well, and they leave you three additional cards to play with. So the best options use lengths with no common factors. The winner is 5 + 3 + 2 = 10, which takes 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 shuffles.
paras.zh: 长度具有共同因子的循环废卡。例如，四轮和六轮洗牌后，洗牌 12 次后都会恢复原状，但四轮和三轮也一样，并且它们会为您留下三张额外的牌可以玩。因此，最好的选择是使用没有公因数的长度。获胜者是 5 + 3 + 2 = 10，需要 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 次洗牌。

paras.en: Fun fact: for a full deck of 52 cards, the longest shuffle uses cycles of length four, five, seven, nine, 11 and 13, plus three cards that stay in their original positions, and it takes 180,180 shuffles to restore the deck.
paras.zh: 有趣的事实：对于一整副 52 张牌，最长的洗牌需要使用长度为 4、5、7、9、11 和 13 的循环，加上保留在原始位置的三张牌，需要 180,180 次洗牌才能恢复这副牌。

paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

articles.title: Two stars in the Andromeda galaxy merged before astronomers’ eyes
articles.author: Meghan Bartels

paras.en: For seven years, a giant star in the Andromeda galaxy grew brighter. It swelled to more than twice its original size, even as its surface temperature barely changed. Then, in October 2025, it erupted. The slow brightening and sudden eruption tell a story of a smaller star orbiting inside of a massive star and what became of the pair, researchers report November 18 in Nature.
paras.zh: 七年来，仙女座星系中的一颗巨星变得越来越亮。尽管其表面温度几乎没有变化，但它膨胀到原来大小的两倍多。然后，2025年10月，它爆发了。研究人员于 11 月 18 日在《自然》杂志上报道，缓慢的变亮和突然的喷发讲述了一颗较小的恒星在一颗大质量恒星内部运行的故事，以及这对恒星后来的演变。

paras.en: In work published last year, after poring through nearly 30 years of telescope data, astronomers had found that the giant began brightening in 2018 and proposed that a smaller star was circling ever closer around a giant companion and had even slipped inside its outermost layers. Astronomers call this elusive phase of a binary star’s life common-envelope evolution.
paras.zh: 在去年发表的研究中，天文学家在仔细研究了近 30 年的望远镜数据后发现，这颗巨星在 2018 年开始变亮，并提出一颗较小的恒星正在围绕一颗巨大的伴星旋转得越来越近，甚至滑入了它的最外层。天文学家将双星生命中这个难以捉摸的阶段称为共包层演化。

paras.en: Now, the astronomers have analyzed the system’s dramatic next developments, culminating in the October 2025 eruption. (The stars are nicknamed Little Bao and Big Bao as a nod to that event’s official designation, AT 2025abao.)
paras.zh: 现在，天文学家已经分析了该系统接下来的戏剧性发展，最终导致 2025 年 10 月的喷发。 （这些明星被昵称为“小包”和“大包”，以纪念该赛事的官方名称 AT 2025abao。）

paras.en: First, astrophysicist Viraj Karambelkar of Columbia University and colleagues revisited those years of brightening given the imminent eruption. One cause of the brightening could have been gas flowing away from the stars, giving off light as it slowed down. But even if all the energy of that moving gas turned into light, it still wouldn’t be enough to explain the glow.
paras.zh: 首先，哥伦比亚大学的天体物理学家维拉吉·卡拉姆贝尔卡（Viraj Karambelkar）及其同事在即将爆发的情况下重新审视了那些年的明亮现象。变亮的原因之一可能是气体从恒星流走，在减速时发出光。但即使移动气体的所有能量都转化为光，仍然不足以解释这种发光。

paras.en: Instead, the researchers determined that the binary hypothesis they had originally proposed fit better: As Little Bao orbited inside Big Bao’s gas outer layers, the gas pushed back against the little star. That drag made Little Bao spiral inward and transfer energy to the surrounding gas. Some of that energy escaped as light, making Big Bao shine brighter.
paras.zh: 相反，研究人员认为他们最初提出的二元假设更适合：当小包在大包的气体外层内绕轨道运行时，气体向后推小恒星。那股阻力让小宝向内盘旋，将能量传递给周围的气体。一些能量以光的形式逸出，使大包变得更加明亮。

paras.en: Then, it was time to dig into what caused the eruption. If the outburst threw enough of the shared gas into space, the individual stars could have survived in an even tighter orbit. But the team estimates that only about a tenth of the giant’s outer gas escaped. The energy carried by that fast-moving gas also suggests that Little Bao reached Big Bao’s core. Together, those clues point to a merger.
paras.zh: 然后，是时候深入研究导致火山爆发的原因了。如果爆发将足够多的共享气体抛入太空，那么单个恒星就可以在更紧密的轨道上幸存下来。但研究小组估计，只有大约十分之一的巨人外部气体逸出。那种快速移动的气体所携带的能量也表明小包到达了大包的核心。所有这些线索都指向合并。

paras.en: Still, too much dust clouds the system to directly see what remains. And it won’t settle for years or even decades, although Karambelkar and his colleagues will be watching.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，太多的灰尘覆盖了系统，无法直接看到剩下的东西。尽管卡拉姆贝尔卡和他的同事们会密切关注，但这种情况在几年甚至几十年内都不会解决。

paras.en: They’ll be looking for more examples of this type of merger, too. “Now we can go and try to look for similar systems,” Karambelkar says, “and hopefully aim to catch more of these systems even before they erupt.”
paras.zh: 他们还将寻找更多此类合并的例子。卡拉姆贝尔卡说：“现在我们可以尝试寻找类似的系统，并希望能够在更多的系统爆发之前捕获它们。”

articles.title: A fast-growing heart is good for the Grinch. People are another story
articles.author: Tina Hesman Saey

paras.en: In the classic Dr. Seuss tale, How the Grinch Stole Christmas, the Grinch starts out with a heart “two sizes too small.” He’s a mean one, disguising himself as Santa Claus and stealing all the Whos’ toys, food and decorations. Poised to throw it all off a mountain, the grumpy loner has a change of heart as joyous song rises from Whoville.
paras.zh: 在苏斯博士的经典故事《格林奇如何偷走圣诞节》中，格林奇一开始的心“小了两号”。他是一个卑鄙的人，伪装成圣诞老人并偷走了谁的所有玩具、食物和装饰品。当欢乐的歌声从 Whoville 中响起时，这位脾气暴躁的孤独者准备将一切从山上扔下来，但他的心却改变了。

paras.en: “They say that the Grinch’s small heart grew three sizes that day,” giving him “the strength of 10 Grinches plus two,” says the narrator of the 1966 movie version. With a beatific smile, he pulls the stolen goods back from the brink and returns everything.
paras.zh: 1966 年电影版本的旁白说道：“据说，那天格林奇的小心脏长大了三倍，”赋予了他“10 个格林奇加两个的力量”。他带着幸福的微笑，将赃物从悬崖边拉了回来，并归还了所有东西。

paras.en: Would a too-small heart make you grumpy like the Grinch? And what would happen if your heart went from too small to really big in an instant? The answer depends on what causes the heart to shrink or swell, experts say. And whether or not you are a snake.
paras.zh: 心太小会让你像格林奇一样脾气暴躁吗？如果你的心在一瞬间从太小变成了很大，会发生什么？专家说，答案取决于导致心脏收缩或肿胀的原因。以及无论你是不是蛇。

paras.en: Heart size is generally pegged to body size, says Michelle Kittleson, a cardiologist at Cedars Sinai Smidt Heart Institute in Los Angeles. Bigger people tend to have bigger hearts. But some people, she says, have hearts that are naturally bigger or smaller than average for their bodies. It’s not clear why. However, she says, “there are negative consequences of having a too-small heart.”
paras.zh: 洛杉矶雪松西奈史密斯心脏研究所的心脏病专家米歇尔·基特尔森说，心脏的大小通常与身体的大小挂钩。更大的人往往有更大的心。但她说，有些人的心脏天生就比身体的平均水平更大或更小。目前尚不清楚原因。然而，她说，“心脏太小会产生负面后果。”

paras.en: In one 2025 study, researchers looked at medical records from more than 360,000 people in Australia. Those with smaller-than-average hearts had a higher risk of dying within five years than people with average or larger hearts, the team reported in JACC: Advances.
paras.zh: 在 2025 年的一项研究中，研究人员查看了澳大利亚超过 360,000 人的医疗记录。研究小组在《JACC：进展》中报告称，心脏小于平均水平的人五年内死亡的风险高于心脏平均或较大的人。

paras.en: Smaller hearts may not pump blood as well as larger ones, making it harder for people to exercise. And if the Grinch didn’t exercise enough, maybe “then that made him really tired, and that made him grumpy,” Kittleson says. “Or maybe he did the research, and he found out that his life expectancy was shortened because of it, and that made him even grumpier.”
paras.zh: 较小的心脏可能无法像较大的心脏那样泵血，这使得人们更难锻炼。如果格林奇没有进行足够的锻炼，也许“那会让他真的很累，而且会让他脾气暴躁，”基特尔森说。 “或者也许他做了研究，发现他的预期寿命因此而缩短，这让他变得更加脾气暴躁。”

paras.en: But would rapidly increasing his heart’s size be good for the Grinch?
paras.zh: 但迅速增大心脏大小对格林奇有好处吗？

paras.en: As the Grinch slides downhill toward Whoville, pulled by a sled piled high with presents he’d stolen and now was returning, he physically undergoes a change. What started as a heart two sizes too small swelled three sizes, both curing his grumpiness and giving him super strength. Or so the classic tale goes. A person going through such a dramatic change may not fare as well.
paras.zh: 当圣诞怪杰拉着雪橇滑下山坡，前往沃维尔时，雪橇上堆满了他偷来的礼物，现在又要回来了，他的身体发生了变化。原本小了两颗的心脏后来膨胀了三颗，既治愈了他的脾气，又给了他超强的力量。或者说这个经典故事是这样的。经历如此巨大变化的人可能不会有同样的表现。

paras.en: There are many ways a heart can grow, says Leslie Leinwand, a molecular biologist and geneticist at the University of Colorado Boulder. With vigorous exercise, “your heart gets bigger in good ways,” Leinwand says. That can be true for athletes who do lots of cardio, such as swimmers and marathon runners.
paras.zh: 科罗拉多大学博尔德分校的分子生物学家和遗传学家莱斯利·莱因万德 (Leslie Leinwand) 表示，心脏的生长方式有很多种。莱因万德说，通过剧烈运动，“你的心脏会以良好的方式变大”。对于经常进行有氧运动的运动员来说确实如此，例如游泳运动员和马拉松运动员。

paras.en: “Their heart gets bigger and thicker,” Kittleson says. “But it’s a good thing in them because it helps them pump more blood per minute than someone with a normal-size heart.” Pregnancy also makes the whole organ expand to boost blood to the developing fetus. If people stop exercising, or give birth, their hearts will shrink back to normal size within months.
paras.zh: “他们的心变得更大、更厚，”基特森说。 “但这对他们来说是一件好事，因为它可以帮助他们比心脏大小正常的人每分钟泵出更多的血液。”怀孕还会使整个器官扩张，为发育中的胎儿提供血液。如果人们停止锻炼或分娩，他们的心脏会在几个月内缩小到正常大小。

paras.en: Some diseases, though, can enlarge hearts in deadly ways. “If you’ve got untreated high blood pressure,” Leinwand says, “you can get a huge heart, and it’s not good for you.”
paras.zh: 然而，有些疾病可以致命地扩大心脏。 “如果你患有高血压而未经治疗，”莱因万德说，“你的心脏可能会变大，但这对你没有好处。”

paras.en: Stress, bad heart valves and some genetic diseases can also result in bigger, but weaker, hearts. In those cases, the heart muscle grows in order to pump more blood. At the same time, the inside of the left ventricle — the heart chamber that pumps oxygenated blood to the body — can shrink. That makes it harder for the heart to push blood out. This kind of growth takes time, Kittleson says.
paras.zh: 压力、心脏瓣膜不良和一些遗传疾病也会导致心脏变大但更弱。在这些情况下，心肌会生长以泵出更多血液。与此同时，左心室（将含氧血液泵送到身体的心室）内部会收缩。这使得心脏更难将血液排出。基特森说，这种增长需要时间。

paras.en: There is one rare condition in which the heart can inflate suddenly. Called takotsubo or stress cardiomyopathy — or in some cases, broken-heart syndrome — it is brought on by extreme stress. That can include positive things like winning the lottery or entering a surprise party or negative stress such as break-up or losing a job.
paras.zh: 有一种罕见的情况，心脏会突然膨胀。这种病被称为“章鱼壶”或应激性心肌病，或者在某些情况下被称为“心碎综合症”，是由极端压力引起的。这可以包括积极的事情，例如中彩票或参加惊喜派对，也可以包括消极的压力，例如分手或失业。

paras.en: A surge of epinephrine, or adrenaline, from stress can make the left ventricle bulge into the shape of a pot used to catch octopuses. (Takotsubo is Japanese for “octopus pot.”) That causes immediate heart failure as the heart chamber gets too big to pump blood.
paras.zh: 压力造成的肾上腺素激增会使左心室膨胀成用来捕捉章鱼的锅的形状。 （Takotsubo 在日语中是“章鱼锅”的意思。）这会导致立即心力衰竭，因为心室变得太大而无法泵血。

paras.en: So instead of becoming super strong, the Grinch “would have keeled over and collapsed,” Kittleson says. (People can survive with prompt medical care and their hearts can return to normal size in a few months.)
paras.zh: 因此，格林奇不但不会变得超级强大，反而“会翻倒并倒塌，”基特森说。 （人们可以通过及时的医疗护理生存，并且他们的心脏可以在几个月内恢复到正常大小。）

paras.en: Given the Grinch survived his rapid growth, there’s another possible scenario: Maybe his heart is more like a snake’s.
paras.zh: 鉴于格林奇在他的快速成长中幸存下来，还有另一种可能的情况：也许他的心脏更像是一条蛇的心脏。

paras.en: Pythons’ hearts can balloon by up to 25 percent in a day after the snakes eat a large meal — sometimes as big as an adult deer. And the bigger a python’s meal, the more its heart grows. Larger hearts pump blood with more force, Leinwand and her colleagues reported in 2024 in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The researchers don’t know if this makes the snakes stronger overall.
paras.zh: 在吃完一顿大餐后，蟒蛇的心脏在一天内会膨胀高达 25%（有时和成年鹿一样大）。蟒蛇吃的食物越多，它的心脏就越长大。 Leinwand 和她的同事于 2024 年在《美国国家科学院院刊》上报道称，心脏越大，泵血的力量就越大。研究人员不知道这是否会让蛇整体变得更强。

paras.en: Once a meal is digested, the heart shrinks again. Snakes can go through many shrink-and-grow cycles with no ill effect. Leinwand hopes that studying these snakes will lead to treatments that make human hearts healthier.
paras.zh: 一旦食物被消化，心脏就会再次收缩。蛇可以经历许多收缩和生长的周期，而不会产生不良影响。莱因万德希望通过研究这些蛇能够找到使人类心脏更健康的治疗方法。

paras.en: But becoming kinder, like the Grinch? Maybe not.
paras.zh: 但变得更友善，就像格林奇一样？也许不是。

paras.en: Notes Leinwand, “our snakes, when they eat a lot, they get rather aggressive.”
paras.zh: Leinwand 指出，“我们的蛇如果吃得太多，就会变得相当具有攻击性。”

articles.title: This year’s El Niño is unlike any other on record
articles.author: Nikk Ogasa

paras.en: It was an unprecedented year for El Niño, the weather-changing ocean pattern defined by warmer-than-normal surface waters in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific. By October 18, the ocean area that researchers use to monitor El Niño’s severity climbed to an average temperature of over 30° Celsius (86° Fahrenheit) for the first time in history. From there, it kept on rising.
paras.zh: 对于厄尔尼诺现象来说，今年是史无前例的一年，厄尔尼诺现象是一种改变天气的海洋模式，其特征是赤道太平洋中部和东部的地表水温高于正常水平。到 10 月 18 日，研究人员用来监测厄尔尼诺现象严重程度的海域平均温度历史上首次攀升至 30 摄氏度（86 华氏度）以上。从那时起，它继续上涨。

paras.en: In September, the region’s daily average sea surface temperature reached the most extreme level ever recorded: more than 3.03 degrees Celsius above the 30-year average (dashed line). The World Meteorological Organization predicts that sea surface temperatures may peak at 3.7 degrees above that average by January. The two previous strongest El Niños on record emerged in 1997 and 2015.
paras.zh: 9月，该地区日平均海面温度达到有记录以来的最极端水平：比30年平均水平（虚线）高出3.03摄氏度以上。世界气象组织预测，到 1 月份，海面温度可能会达到峰值，比平均水平高出 3.7 度。有记录以来前两次最强的厄尔尼诺现象分别出现在 1997 年和 2015 年。

paras.en: All that hot water has fueled the most active Pacific hurricane season on record. By mid-October, 331 units of cyclone energy had accumulated, beating out 2018’s record of 318 units. It has also unleashed heat into the atmosphere, affecting distant circulation patterns and leading to an extraordinarily quiet Atlantic hurricane season.
paras.zh: 所有这些热水都助长了有记录以来最活跃的太平洋飓风季节。截至 10 月中旬，旋风能量已累积 331 单位，打破了 2018 年 318 单位的记录。它还向大气中释放热量，影响遥远的环流模式，导致大西洋飓风季节异常安静。

paras.en: 2026’s El Niño will be felt well beyond the New Year. Precipitation and drought impacts are expected across the world through spring 2027. And the global heating effect could compound with human-caused climate warming to make 2027 the hottest year ever recorded.
paras.zh: 2026 年的厄尔尼诺现象在新年之后仍将存在。预计到 2027 年春季，全球都会遭受降水和干旱影响。全球变暖效应可能与人为造成的气候变暖相结合，使 2027 年成为有记录以来最热的一年。

paras.en: The heat that El Niño unleashes into the atmosphere shifts storm tracks and weather patterns globally. Here are some of the most significant observed and anticipated effects.
paras.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象释放到大气中的热量改变了全球风暴路径和天气模式。以下是一些最显着的观察到和预期的影响。

articles.title: One Form of Exercise Improves Sleep The Most, Research Shows
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: Scientists know exercise is an important factor in getting a good night's sleep, but it's unclear which types of exercise have the greatest effects.
paras.zh: 科学家知道运动是获得良好睡眠的重要因素，但尚不清楚哪种类型的运动效果最大。

paras.en: From resistance training and HIIT (high-intensity interval training) to tai chi and Pilates, research is beginning to show that not all forms of exercise are created equal when it comes to tackling sleep disruption.
paras.zh: 从阻力训练和 HIIT（高强度间歇训练）到太极拳和普拉提，研究开始表明，在解决睡眠干扰问题方面，并非所有形式的运动都是相同的。

paras.en: A recent meta-analysis published in Sleep and Biological Rhythms compared different workouts according to their effects on sleep, and identified one stand-out: high-intensity yoga.
paras.zh: 最近发表在《睡眠与生物节律》上的一项荟萃​​分析根据不同的锻炼对睡眠的影响进行了比较，并发现了一种突出的方法：高强度瑜伽。

paras.en: Bringing together data from 30 randomized controlled trials, researchers at Harbin Sport University in China found that regular yoga has the strongest association with improvements to sleep, over walking, combination exercise, aerobic exercise, or traditional Chinese exercises, like qi gong and tai chi.
paras.zh: 中国哈尔滨体育大学的研究人员汇集了 30 项随机对照试验的数据，发现定期瑜伽与改善睡眠、过度步行、组合运动、有氧运动或气功和太极拳等中国传统运动的关联最强。

paras.en: The trials involved over 2,500 adults with sleep disturbances across a wide range of ages, from around a dozen countries and regions.
paras.zh: 这些试验涉及来自十几个国家和地区的 2,500 多名不同年龄段、患有睡眠障碍的成年人。

paras.en: Of all forms of exercise included in the study, the researchers found that two high-intensity yoga sessions each week, lasting up to 30 minutes, were the "optimal exercise prescription" for poor sleep.
paras.zh: 在研究中包含的所有形式的运动中，研究人员发现，每周两次高强度瑜伽课程，持续时间长达 30 分钟，是睡眠不佳的“最佳运动处方”。

paras.en: Watch the clip below for a summary of the research:
paras.zh: 观看下面的剪辑以了解研究摘要：

paras.en: "This research encompassed a comprehensive analysis of 30 studies that systematically evaluated the impact of various exercise regimens on enhancing the sleep quality of individuals experiencing sleep disturbances using network meta-analysis techniques," the researchers concluded.
paras.zh: 研究人员总结道：“这项研究对 30 项研究进行了全面分析，这些研究使用网络荟萃分析技术系统地评估了各种运动方案对提高睡眠障碍患者睡眠质量的影响。”

paras.en: "The findings suggest that a yoga exercise prescription, conducted twice weekly for 8–10 weeks, lasting ≤ 30 min per session, and of high intensity, is the most effective approach for improving the sleep quality of individuals with sleep disturbances."
paras.zh: “研究结果表明，每周两次、持续 8-10 周、每次持续 ≤ 30 分钟、高强度的瑜伽运动处方是改善睡眠障碍患者睡眠质量的最有效方法。”

paras.en: This optimal exercise prescription is actually quite distinct from the gentle, slow movements you might associate with yoga.
paras.zh: 这种最佳的运动处方实际上与瑜伽中温和、缓慢的运动截然不同。

paras.en: High-intensity yoga involves a much faster flow between poses that harness your own body weight to create resistance.
paras.zh: 高强度瑜伽涉及姿势之间的更快流动，利用您自己的体重来产生阻力。

paras.en: Next in the ranks was walking, followed by resistance training (also known as strength training, which includes workouts like Pilates and weight lifting).
paras.zh: 接下来是步行，然后是阻力训练（也称为力量训练，包括普拉提和举重等锻炼）。

paras.en: The researchers also found that the yoga regimen that worked best to improve sleep had a "significantly superior" effect compared to aerobic exercise.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现，与有氧运动相比，最能改善睡眠的瑜伽疗法具有“显着优越”的效果。

paras.en: That result contrasts with the findings of another review, published in 2023, that found three sessions of aerobic or mid-intensity exercise each week could be the most effective workout for addressing sleep disturbances.
paras.zh: 这一结果与 2023 年发表的另一篇评论的结果形成鲜明对比，该评论发现每周进行 3 次有氧或中等强度运动可能是解决睡眠障碍的最有效锻炼方法。

paras.en: One study included in that review, however, did indicate that yoga had more significant effects on sleep outcomes than other exercise types.
paras.zh: 然而，该评论中包含的一项研究确实表明，瑜伽对睡眠结果的影响比其他运动类型更显着。

paras.en: Yoga can also be difficult to categorize as either aerobic or anaerobic, and its intensity can vary depending on the technique used.
paras.zh: 瑜伽也很难归类为有氧或无氧，并且其强度可能会根据所使用的技术而有所不同。

paras.en: The same goes for other exercises that have been identified as helpful in similar studies: tai chi, Pilates, and aerobic exercise, for instance.
paras.zh: 这同样适用于类似研究中被认为有帮助的其他运动：例如太极、普拉提和有氧运动。

paras.en: Perhaps these differences in practice – and definition – can explain why the outcomes differ from trial to trial.
paras.zh: 也许这些实践和定义上的差异可以解释为什么每次试验的结果都不同。

paras.en: A study published in 2025 found that tai chi was effective for improving sleep, with results on par with cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I).
paras.zh: 2025 年发表的一项研究发现，太极拳可有效改善睡眠，其效果与失眠认知行为疗法 (CBT-I) 相当。

paras.en: In the short term, a group of participants who received CBT-I reported a greater reduction in their insomnia symptoms than those in a tai chi group, but when the researchers assessed participants again 15 months later, the tai chi group had 'caught up'.
paras.zh: 在短期内，接受 CBT-I 的一组参与者报告说，他们的失眠症状比太极拳组有更大程度的减轻，但当研究人员 15 个月后再次评估参与者时，太极拳组已经“迎头赶上了”。

paras.en: The authors of that study suggested tai chi's accessibility and ease of integration into people's lifestyles may benefit its long-term effectiveness.
paras.zh: 该研究的作者认为，太极拳的普及性和易于融入人们的生活方式可能有利于其长期有效性。

paras.en: These meta-analyses cannot explain why yoga or other forms of exercise may be particularly beneficial for sleep, but there are a few possibilities.
paras.zh: 这些荟萃分析无法解释为什么瑜伽或其他形式的运动可能对睡眠特别有益，但有一些可能性。

paras.en: Yoga is known to raise the heart rate, push muscles, and regulate breathing (something it has in common with tai chi and Pilates).
paras.zh: 众所周知，瑜伽可以提高心率、推动肌肉和调节呼吸（这与太极拳和普拉提有共同点）。

paras.en: Research suggests breath control can activate the parasympathetic nervous system by stimulating the vagus nerve, and improve sleep quality.
paras.zh: 研究表明，呼吸控制可以通过刺激迷走神经来激活副交感神经系统，从而改善睡眠质量。

paras.en: Other studies even suggest yoga regulates brainwave activity patterns, which could promote deeper sleep.
paras.zh: 其他研究甚至表明瑜伽可以调节脑电波活动模式，从而促进更深的睡眠。

paras.en: And, again and again, the research highlights forms of exercise that involve resistance (even ones that aren't specifically labeled 'resistance training').
paras.zh: 而且，研究一次又一次地强调了涉及阻力的运动形式（即使是那些没有专门标记为“阻力训练”的运动）。

paras.en: These workouts, in which your muscles are working against an oppositional force (think downward dog, plank, reformer Pilates, and weights), could be best for a good night's sleep.
paras.zh: 在这些锻炼中，你的肌肉会对抗相反的力量（比如下犬式、平板支撑、普拉提普拉提和举重），可能最适合睡个好觉。

paras.en: Perhaps sweating it out on a yoga mat works because it deliberately pairs breath control with resistance – but we'll need some more detailed studies to know for sure.
paras.zh: 也许在瑜伽垫上出汗是有效的，因为它故意将呼吸控制与阻力结合起来——但我们需要一些更详细的研究才能确定。

paras.en: There's no shortage of evidence telling us exercise in general will help your sleep, but rigorous studies on specific exercises and their long-term effects are lacking.
paras.zh: 不乏证据告诉我们，一般运动有助于睡眠，但缺乏对特定运动及其长期影响的严格研究。

paras.en: "Caution should be exercised when interpreting findings from studies on sleep disturbances, given the limited number of studies included and the unique characteristics of the sleep disturbances population," explain the researchers at Harbin Sport University.
paras.zh: 哈尔滨体育大学的研究人员解释说：“考虑到纳入的研究数量有限以及睡眠障碍人群的独特特征，在解释睡眠障碍研究结果时应谨慎。”

paras.en: "Further, high-quality research is needed to confirm these findings."
paras.zh: “此外，需要高质量的研究来证实这些发现。”

paras.en: Related: This One Sleep Factor Matters More Than How Many Hours You Get, Study Suggests
paras.zh: 相关：研究表明，这一睡眠因素比您获得多少小时更重​​要

paras.en: Every body and brain is different: there's no guaranteed one-size-fits-all solution to insomnia or other sleep disturbances.
paras.zh: 每个人的身体和大脑都是不同的：对于失眠或其他睡眠障碍，没有一种万能的解决方案。

paras.en: While exercise could be one part of the puzzle, it's best to speak with a doctor if your quality of life is being affected by sleep disturbances.
paras.zh: 虽然锻炼可能是这个难题的一部分，但如果您的生活质量受到睡眠障碍的影响，最好咨询医生。

paras.en: The yoga study was published in Sleep and Biological Rhythms.
paras.zh: 这项瑜伽研究发表在《睡眠与生物节律》上。

articles.title: Severe PMS May Actually Be Three Different Subtypes, Researchers Suggest
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Some menstrual cycles can feel like a physical and emotional rollercoaster ride.
paras.zh: 有些月经周期感觉就像是身体和情绪上的过山车。

paras.en: In severe cases of premenstrual syndrome (PMS), the body is thought to have an abnormal reaction to the rise and fall of estrogen and progesterone.
paras.zh: 在严重的经前综合症（PMS）中，身体被认为对雌激素和孕激素的升降有异常反应。

paras.en: This can lead to a whole host of distressing and overwhelming behavioral and physical symptoms, including anxiety and depression, irritability, fatigue, headaches, bloating, body aches, or sleep issues.
paras.zh: 这可能会导致一系列令人痛苦和难以承受的行为和身体症状，包括焦虑和抑郁、烦躁、疲劳、头痛、腹胀、身体疼痛或睡眠问题。

paras.en: The condition is known as premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), and it is estimated to affect about 3 to 8 percent of those who regularly menstruate.
paras.zh: 这种情况被称为经前焦虑症 (PMDD)，据估计，大约有 3% 至 8% 的月经规律人士患有此病。

paras.en: But it doesn't present the same for everyone – despite the fact that it is often diagnosed and treated that way.
paras.zh: 但它对每个人来说并不都是一样的——尽管事实上它经常被这样诊断和治疗。

paras.en: Researchers at Uppsala University in Sweden have now split the disorder into three different patterns based on when symptoms begin, how severe they become, and how long they last.
paras.zh: 瑞典乌普萨拉大学的研究人员现在根据症状开始的时间、症状的严重程度以及持续的时间，将这种疾病分为三种不同的模式。

paras.en: This new personalized approach could lead to better diagnosis and treatment.
paras.zh: 这种新的个性化方法可以带来更好的诊断和治疗。

paras.en: The team followed 90 women with PMDD and 44 women without the disorder across two consecutive menstrual cycles, tracking their self-reported symptoms from day to day.
paras.zh: 该团队对 90 名患有经前抑郁症的女性和 44 名未患经前抑郁症的女性进行了连续两个月经周期的追踪，每天跟踪她们自我报告的症状。

paras.en: Computer models ultimately unveiled three distinct subtypes for those with PMDD, challenging the assumption that all symptoms follow a similar timeline.
paras.zh: 计算机模型最终揭示了经前抑郁症患者的三种不同亚型，挑战了所有症状都遵循相似时间表的假设。

paras.en: Today, a DSM-5 diagnosis depends on PMDD worsening in the week before menstruation and improving shortly after bleeding begins, but symptoms don't always present this way.
paras.zh: 如今，DSM-5 诊断取决于经前一周恶化的经前抑郁症（PMDD）以及出血开始后不久的改善，但症状并不总是以这种方式出现。

paras.en: The new study suggests there are different timelines for different manifestations of the disorder.
paras.zh: 这项新研究表明，这种疾病的不同表现有不同的时间表。

paras.en: One of the most common symptom timelines identified by researchers in Sweden is called the 'severe full luteal'.
paras.zh: 瑞典研究人员发现的最常见症状时间表之一被称为“严重黄体饱满”。

paras.en: Symptoms in this case usually begin shortly after ovulation, and in the weeks leading up to menstruation, they gradually become more severe. Once bleeding starts, however, symptoms typically cease.
paras.zh: 这种情况下的症状通常在排卵后不久出现，并在月经前几周逐渐变得更加严重。然而，一旦开始出血，症状通常就会消失。

paras.en: Irritability commonly follows this pattern, the authors found.
paras.zh: 作者发现，烦躁通常遵循这种模式。

paras.en: A second pattern, called the 'severe late luteal', has symptoms that begin a bit later in the luteal phase and ramp up quickly to become severe.
paras.zh: 第二种模式称为“严重黄体晚期”，其症状在黄体期稍晚一些开始，并迅速加剧直至变得严重。

paras.en: They also can linger for four to five days after bleeding begins.
paras.zh: 出血后，它们也可能会持续四到五天。

paras.en: Anxiety commonly follows this trajectory.
paras.zh: 焦虑通常遵循这个轨迹。

paras.en: The third and final pattern is the 'moderate late luteal' subtype. In this case, symptoms appear just before menstruation, and they are generally less severe. They also disappear soon after bleeding starts.
paras.zh: 第三种也是最后一种模式是“中晚期黄体”亚型。在这种情况下，症状会在月经前出现，而且通常不太严重。它们也会在出血后很快消失。

paras.en: Depression, anxiety, and mood swings commonly follow this timeline.
paras.zh: 抑郁、焦虑和情绪波动通常遵循这个时间表。

paras.en: As do several physical symptoms, such as joint pain and headaches, though they tend to be less severe than in other timelines.
paras.zh: 关节疼痛和头痛等一些身体症状也是如此，尽管它们往往没有其他时间线那么严重。

paras.en: "To date, PMDD symptomatology and its temporal onset and offset have generally been treated as homogeneous across, and stable within, individuals, with little attention given to inter- and intra-individual heterogeneity," researchers at Uppsala explain.
paras.zh: 乌普萨拉的研究人员解释说：“迄今为止，PMDD 症状及其时间发作和抵消通常被视为个体间同质且稳定，而很少关注个体间和个体内的异质性。”

paras.en: But the reality may be far more nuanced than that, and researchers in Sweden are not the first to delve into the details.
paras.zh: 但现实可能比这要微妙得多，瑞典的研究人员并不是第一个深入研究细节的人。

paras.en: In 2019, an international team of researchers identified three very similar symptom trajectories among 74 individuals prospectively diagnosed with PMDD.
paras.zh: 2019 年，一个国际研究小组在 74 名预期诊断为经前抑郁症 (PMDD) 的人中发现了三种非常相似的症状轨迹。

paras.en: But this previous study only tracked one menstrual cycle.
paras.zh: 但之前的这项研究只追踪了一个月经周期。

paras.en: In the new study from Sweden, two cycles were tracked, and 98 percent of participants with PMDD experienced more than one symptom subtype during this time.
paras.zh: 在瑞典的这项新研究中，跟踪了两个周期，98% 的经前抑郁症参与者在此期间经历了不止一种症状亚型。

paras.en: The study is small, and ovulation wasn't directly measured, but the authors argue that their findings support the idea that PMDD is a "complex, cyclical disorder rooted in psychoneuroendocrine dynamics."
paras.zh: 这项研究规模较小，也没有直接测量排卵，但作者认为，他们的研究结果支持这样的观点，即经前抑郁症是一种“植根于心理神经内分泌动力学的复杂的、周期性的疾病”。

paras.en: "By integrating dynamic symptom modeling with clinical practice, we could advance precision in the mental health care of people who menstruate, and reduce the burden of PMDD," the team argues.
paras.zh: 研究小组认为：“通过将动态症状模型与临床实践相结合，我们可以提高经期患者心理健康护理的精确度，并减轻经前抑郁症的负担。”

paras.en: Similar to severe period pain, PMDD is often dismissed by health care professionals as all part of the typical menstrual cycle.
paras.zh: 与严重的经痛类似，经前抑郁症常常被医疗保健专业人士忽视，认为它是典型月经周期的一部分。

paras.en: But this disorder is not to be taken lightly.
paras.zh: 但这种疾病不能掉以轻心。

paras.en: The emotional, cognitive, and physical symptoms can severely impair a person's ability to function and can cause great distress in their life – even suicidal ideation.
paras.zh: 情绪、认知和身体症状会严重损害一个人的功能能力，并可能给他们的生活带来巨大的痛苦，甚至产生自杀意念。

paras.en: Today, however, awareness of the condition is poor, and misdiagnosis is common.
paras.zh: 然而，如今人们对这种疾病的认识很差，误诊也很常见。

paras.en: Psychiatrists and psychologists often fail to recognize the condition, and for patients in many nations, medical gaslighting and diagnostic 'odysseys' are common experiences.
paras.zh: 精神科医生和心理学家常常无法认识到这种情况，对于许多国家的患者来说，医疗煤气灯和诊断“冒险之旅”是常见的经历。

paras.en: In a 2026 editorial for the British Journal of General Practice, researchers argued that "while there is overlap between PMDD and PMS, and current guidelines largely recommend similar management approaches, the severity and cyclical nature of symptoms may not be fully recognized."
paras.zh: 在《英国全科医学杂志》2026 年的一篇社论中，研究人员认为，“虽然经前抑郁障碍 (PMDD) 和经前综合症 (PMS) 之间存在重叠，并且当前的指南在很大程度上推荐类似的管理方法，但症状的严重性和周期性性质可能尚未得到充分认识。”

paras.en: "As a result," they add, "patients with PMDD may be managed in the same way as those with milder PMS, which may lead to under-recognition of the impact on functioning, delayed escalation of treatment, and a lack of appropriate follow-up."
paras.zh: 他们补充道：“因此，经前抑郁症患者的治疗方式可能与轻度经前综合症患者相同，这可能会导致人们对其功能影响的认识不足、治疗升级延迟以及缺乏适当的随访。”

paras.en: Even when a patient is properly diagnosed, treatment options are limited.
paras.zh: 即使患者得到正确诊断，治疗选择也是有限的。

paras.en: Psychological support, like cognitive behavioral therapy, may be recommended, and pharmacological treatment, such as oral contraceptive pills or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, could be advised.
paras.zh: 可能会建议心理支持，如认知行为疗法，并建议药物治疗，如口服避孕药或选择性血清素再摄取抑制剂。

paras.en: But a significant percentage of patients don't respond to available therapies.
paras.zh: 但很大一部分患者对现有疗法没有反应。

paras.en: Treatment-resistant PMDD can be debilitating and life-threatening. A 2021 meta-analysis in the Journal of Women's Health found that PMDD was associated with nearly sevenfold higher odds of suicide attempts.
paras.zh: 难治性经前抑郁症可能会使人衰弱并危及生命。 《女性健康杂志》2021 年的一项荟萃​​分析发现，经前抑郁症与自杀未遂几率高出近七倍有关。

paras.en: Future studies are needed to understand more about how the symptoms of PMDD manifest and how they might be treated more effectively.
paras.zh: 未来的研究需要更多地了解经前抑郁症的症状如何表现以及如何更有效地治疗它们。

paras.en: But if, going forward, each symptom of PMDD is assumed to have a similar timeline, it may obscure some of the underlying mechanisms at play.
paras.zh: 但如果今后假设经前抑郁症的每种症状都有相似的时间线，那么它可能会掩盖一些起作用的潜在机制。

paras.en: Acknowledging that there are differences could ultimately help explain why some patients respond to treatment, and others do not.
paras.zh: 承认存在差异最终可能有助于解释为什么有些患者对治疗有反应，而另一些患者则没有。

paras.en: The research has been published in Nature Communications.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《自然通讯》上。

articles.title: Physicist Finds a Strange New Solution to Einstein's Equations in Five-Dimensional Spacetime: Black Saturn
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: The geometry of the bog-standard black hole is probably pretty familiar to you: a spherical region of space defined by light's inability to escape it.
paras.zh: 您可能对沼泽标准黑洞的几何形状非常熟悉：由光无法逃脱的球形空间区域定义。

paras.en: But the equations we use to describe our reality aren't as strict as the reality itself seems to be. Einstein's theory of general relativity works excellently to describe spacetime… but it does also allow some far stranger versions of it to exist.
paras.zh: 但我们用来描述现实的方程并不像现实本身看起来那么严格。爱因斯坦的广义相对论非常适合描述时空……但它也确实允许一些更奇怪的版本存在。

paras.en: One such oddity is a five-dimensional black hole that does, in fact, have a hole – one shaped like a donut, or torus. And a second black hole can be plopped in the center, a configuration theoretical physicists call the Black Saturn.
paras.zh: 其中一个奇怪的现象是五维黑洞，它实际上有一个洞——形状像甜甜圈或环面。第二个黑洞可能会出现在中心，理论物理学家将这种结构称为“黑土星”。

paras.en: The first mathematical description of a Black Saturn was published in 2007, but with a limitation: the two black holes could only rotate in one plane.
paras.zh: 对黑土星的第一个数学描述于 2007 年发表，但有一个限制：两个黑洞只能在一个平面上旋转。

paras.en: In five-dimensional spacetime, however, objects can rotate in two independent planes at once. Accounting for both rotations would allow physicists to explore configurations that the original solution couldn't – but the mathematics is considerably more complicated.
paras.zh: 然而，在五维时空中，物体可以同时在两个独立的平面中旋转。考虑到这两种旋转将使物理学家能够探索原始解决方案无法探索的配置，但数学要复杂得多。

paras.en: Theoretical physicist Jay Armas of the University of Amsterdam has now picked up that gauntlet.
paras.zh: 阿姆斯特丹大学的理论物理学家杰伊·阿玛斯现在已经接受了这一挑战。

paras.en: In a preprint uploaded to arXiv, he has laid out a mathematical solution that allows the Black Saturn to rotate in both planes, opening up new possibilities for exploring the strange behavior of gravity in higher-dimensional spacetime.
paras.zh: 在上传到 arXiv 的预印本中，他提出了一个数学解决方案，允许黑土星在两个平面上旋转，为探索高维时空中重力的奇怪行为开辟了新的可能性。

paras.en: "The space of black holes in higher-dimensional vacuum gravity is richer than its four-dimensional counterpart," he writes.
paras.zh: “高维真空引力中的黑洞空间比四维黑洞的空间更丰富，”他写道。

paras.en: The spacetime we currently inhabit has, as far as we know, four dimensions – three spatial, and one temporal. Everything within it is governed by the laws of physics as they operate in those four dimensions.
paras.zh: 据我们所知，我们目前居住的时空有四个维度——三个空间维度和一个时间维度。其中的一切都受物理定律的支配，因为它们在这四个维度中运作。

paras.en: Add one extra spatial dimension, however, and the rules shift. It's not that general relativity has changed; the same underlying principles still apply. But the addition of another dimension permits solutions and geometries that aren't available in just four dimensions.
paras.zh: 然而，增加一个额外的空间维度，规则就会发生变化。这并不是说广义相对论改变了；而是说广义相对论改变了。相同的基本原则仍然适用。但是添加另一个维度可以实现仅在四个维度中无法获得的解决方案和几何形状。

paras.en: In a five-dimensional spacetime, Einstein's equations allow a ring-shaped event horizon to exist. Suddenly, Black Saturns are a thing.
paras.zh: 在五维时空中，爱因斯坦方程允许存在环形事件视界。突然之间，黑土星就成了一个东西。

paras.en: These bizarre objects consist of two separate black holes: a spherical one in the center, and a ring-shaped one encircling it. Each has its own event horizon, the boundary beyond which escaping the black hole would require traveling faster than light (which is impossible).
paras.zh: 这些奇异的物体由两个独立的黑洞组成：一个位于中心的球形黑洞，一个环绕它的环形黑洞。每个都有自己的事件视界，超出该边界逃离黑洞将需要比光更快的速度（这是不可能的）。

paras.en: The ring is held in a delicate balance by its rotation. Without sufficient angular momentum, its own gravity would cause it to collapse; spinning allows it to maintain its unusual shape. Meanwhile, the spherical black hole it girdles is more like the four-dimensional versions we know and love.
paras.zh: 环通过旋转保持微妙的平衡。如果没有足够的角动量，它自身的引力就会导致它塌陷；旋转使其能够保持其不寻常的形状。与此同时，它周围的球形黑洞更像是我们所知道和喜爱的四维版本。

paras.en: But the two black holes aren't entirely independent. Both exist within the same spacetime, and, as with four-dimensional black holes, their gravitational influence extends beyond their event horizons.
paras.zh: 但这两个黑洞并不完全独立。两者都存在于同一时空中，并且与四维黑洞一样，它们的引力影响超出了事件视界。

paras.en: So, as they rotate, they can drag the surrounding spacetime along with them, a phenomenon known as frame dragging.
paras.zh: 因此，当它们旋转时，它们可以拖动周围的时空，这种现象称为参考系拖动。

paras.en: In his new solution, Armas has mathematically described a Black Saturn where both black holes can rotate in both independent planes. It's elegant work.
paras.zh: 在他的新解决方案中，阿玛斯从数学上描述了一个黑色土星，其中两个黑洞都可以在两个独立的平面上旋转。这是一件优雅的工作。

paras.en: But that's far from the sum total of it. The possibilities it reveals – inaccessible in the previous uniplanar model – enter into the realm of the truly bizarre.
paras.zh: 但这远非其总和。它所揭示的可能性——在以前的单平面模型中无法实现——进入了真正奇异的领域。

paras.en: For example, black holes have limits to how much angular momentum they can possess relative to their mass. When a black hole reaches that limit, it enters a state known as extremality, in which its Hawking temperature drops to absolute zero.
paras.zh: 例如，黑洞相对于其质量所能拥有的角动量是有限的。当黑洞达到该极限时，它会进入一种称为极值的状态，其中霍金温度降至绝对零。

paras.en: That means it emits none of the Hawking radiation generated by quantum interactions near the event horizon.
paras.zh: 这意味着它不会发射事件视界附近量子相互作用产生的霍金辐射。

paras.en: In five-dimensional spacetime, however, a black hole needs to rotate in both independent planes to reach extremality without its event horizon disappearing altogether.
paras.zh: 然而，在五维时空中，黑洞需要在两个独立平面上旋转才能达到极值，而其事件视界又不会完全消失。

paras.en: Armas's solution shows that both black holes in a Black Saturn can reach extremality simultaneously, each retaining its own event horizon.
paras.zh: 阿马斯的解决方案表明，黑土星中的两个黑洞可以同时达到极值，每个黑洞都保留自己的事件视界。

paras.en: It's the first known exact mathematical solution to Einstein's equations showing that two separate black holes can exist together in this state in an otherwise empty five-dimensional spacetime.
paras.zh: 这是爱因斯坦方程的第一个已知的精确数学解，表明两个独立的黑洞可以在这种状态下同时存在于一个空的五维时空中。

paras.en: But even though both black holes have a Hawking temperature of absolute zero, they can't achieve complete equilibrium.
paras.zh: 但即使两个黑洞的霍金温度都为零，它们也无法达到完全平衡。

paras.en: That's because equilibrium also requires their rotations to match in both planes – something Armas found they cannot do while maintaining a regular Black Saturn configuration.
paras.zh: 这是因为平衡还要求它们在两个平面上的旋转相匹配——阿玛斯发现它们在保持常规的黑土星配置时无法做到这一点。

paras.en: Here's the really delicious part. Each black hole can have its own intrinsic rotation – but because they drag on the spacetime around them, the surrounding ring can induce a rotation of the central black hole's event horizon, even in a plane where that black hole has no angular momentum of its own.
paras.zh: 这是真正美味的部分。每个黑洞都可以有自己的内在旋转，但由于它们拖动周围的时空，周围的环可以引起中心黑洞事件视界的旋转，即使在黑洞本身没有角动量的平面上也是如此。

paras.en: Of course, there's no evidence that Black Saturns actually exist, or that our Universe is somehow hiding the extra spatial dimension needed to accommodate them.
paras.zh: 当然，没有证据表明黑土星确实存在，或者我们的宇宙以某种方式隐藏了容纳它们所需的额外空间维度。

paras.en: But solutions like this offer physicists a way to explore the possibilities of general relativity – put earlier predictions to new tests, and investigate how gravity behaves under conditions vastly different from those we observe.
paras.zh: 但像这样的解决方案为物理学家提供了一种探索广义相对论可能性的方法——将早期的预测付诸新的测试，并研究重力在与我们观察到的条件截然不同的条件下如何表现。

paras.en: Armas's work also lays the groundwork for future research into the behavior of light and matter around these strange configurations, and even the geometry of the spacetime inside their event horizons.
paras.zh: 阿玛斯的工作还为未来研究这些奇怪结构周围的光和物质的行为，甚至是事件视界内的时空几何形状奠定了基础。

paras.en: And it leaves us with the dream of a strange realm beyond our ken, full of black hole donuts and their black hole donut holes.
paras.zh: 它给我们留下了一个超出我们视野的奇怪领域的梦想，那里充满了黑洞甜甜圈和黑洞甜甜圈洞。

paras.en: That, and an absolute rip-snorter of a symphonic metal band name.
paras.zh: 那，以及一个绝对令人窒息的交响金属乐队的名字。

articles.title: After 8 years in space, a groundbreaking X-ray telescope finally opens its eyes

paras.en: After 8 years in space, a groundbreaking X-ray telescope finally opens its eyes
paras.zh: 在太空呆了 8 年之后，突破性的 X 射线望远镜终于睁开了眼睛

paras.en: - After eight years and 10 billion kilometers in space, a groundbreaking X-ray telescope heading to Mercury has captured its first cosmic observations and is performing even better than scientists expected. The instrument could soon reveal Mercury's hidden chemical secrets and transform our understanding of how the solar system's smallest planet formed.
paras.zh: - 经过 8 年和 100 亿公里的太空探索，一架前往水星的突破性 X 射线望远镜首次进行了宇宙观测，其表现甚至比科学家预期的还要好。该仪器很快就会揭示水星隐藏的化学秘密，并改变我们对太阳系最小行星如何形成的理解。

paras.en: After eight years in space and a journey covering 10 billion kilometers, a pioneering X-ray telescope traveling to Mercury has captured its first observations of a distant cosmic object. The instrument, built in the UK, successfully detected X-rays from the Crab Nebula, one of the brightest X-ray sources in the sky, marking an important milestone for the European Space Agency (ESA) and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's BepiColombo mission.
paras.zh: 经过八年的太空旅行和 100 亿公里的旅程，一架前往水星的开创性 X 射线望远镜首次观测到了一个遥远的宇宙物体。该仪器在英国制造，成功探测到来自蟹状星云的 X 射线，蟹状星云是天空中最亮的 X 射线源之一，标志着欧洲航天局 (ESA) 和日本宇宙航空研究开发机构的 BepiColombo 任务的一个重要里程碑。

paras.en: Scientists at the University of Leicester are now evaluating the Mercury Imaging X-ray Spectrometer (MIXS), which is traveling aboard the two-spacecraft mission. Their initial results are highly encouraging, arriving just as BepiColombo prepares to enter orbit around Mercury on November 21.
paras.zh: 莱斯特大学的科学家目前正在评估水星成像 X 射线光谱仪 (MIXS)，该仪器正在执行两艘航天器任务。他们的初步结果非常令人鼓舞，就在 BepiColombo 准备于 11 月 21 日进入水星轨道时得出。

paras.en: The telescope has spent eight years traveling through space, making it essential to confirm that its delicate components are still working properly. Although engineers monitored MIXS throughout the journey, the instrument could not look directly into space until September. That opportunity came after the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) separated from the two science orbiters, the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and Mercury Magnetosphere Orbiter (MMO) or Mio.
paras.zh: 该望远镜已经在太空中旅行了八年，因此有必要确认其精密部件是否仍然正常工作。尽管工程师在整个旅程中对 MIXS 进行了监控，但该仪器直到 9 月份才能够直接观察太空。这个机会是在水星转移舱（MTM）与两个科学轨道飞行器——水星行星轨道飞行器（MPO）和水星磁层轨道飞行器（MMO）或Mio分离后出现的。

paras.en: With its view finally unobstructed, MIXS could begin the critical tests needed before the spacecraft enters its planned orbit around the solar system's smallest planet.
paras.zh: 随着视野最终畅通无阻，MIXS 可以在航天器进入围绕太阳系最小行星的计划轨道之前开始所需的关键测试。

paras.en: A Telescope's First Look Across 6,500 Light-Years
paras.zh: 望远镜首次观测 6,500 光年范围

paras.en: For its first astronomical target, the team selected the Crab Nebula, located approximately 6,500 light-years from Earth. This well-studied remnant of an exploded star produces a strong, predictable X-ray signal, making it an ideal reference for testing the telescope's performance.
paras.zh: 该团队选择了距地球约 6,500 光年的蟹状星云作为其第一个天文目标。这个经过充分研究的恒星爆炸遗迹会产生强烈的、可预测的 X 射线信号，使其成为测试望远镜性能的理想参考。

paras.en: By examining how MIXS observes this distant object, researchers can determine whether the instrument still performs as expected after its lengthy journey. They can also compare the results with laboratory measurements collected in 2015, when the telescope was last tested on Earth.
paras.zh: 通过检查 MIXS 如何观察这个遥远的物体，研究人员可以确定该仪器在漫长的旅程后是否仍能按预期运行。他们还可以将结果与 2015 年（该望远镜最后一次在地球上进行测试）收集的实验室测量结果进行比较。

paras.en: The main observation campaign took place on September 11 and 12. Over 39 hours, the spacecraft carried out 55 carefully controlled changes in orientation to collect the data.
paras.zh: 主要观测活动于 9 月 11 日至 12 日进行。在 39 个小时的时间里，航天器进行了 55 次精心控制的方向变化以收集数据。

paras.en: One important measurement was the telescope's angular resolution, which describes its ability to distinguish small details in an image. Scientists determined this by examining how widely the Crab Nebula's X-ray signal spread across the detector. Remarkably, MIXS delivered slightly sharper resolution than it had during its laboratory tests in 2015.
paras.zh: 一项重要的测量是望远镜的角分辨率，它描述了它区分图像中小细节的能力。科学家通过检查蟹状星云的 X 射线信号在探测器上传播的范围来确定这一点。值得注意的是，MIXS 提供的分辨率比 2015 年实验室测试时的分辨率略高。

paras.en: That improvement is particularly encouraging because the instrument will eventually use its X-ray vision to investigate the composition of Mercury's surface.
paras.zh: 这一改进尤其令人鼓舞，因为该仪器最终将利用其 X 射线视觉来研究水星表面的成分。

paras.en: Better Than Expected After Eight Years in Space
paras.zh: 太空八年后的表现好于预期

paras.en: Professor Emma Bunce, Principal Investigator (PI) for MIXS and Director of the Institute for Space at the University of Leicester, welcomed the results as a major achievement for the international team responsible for developing the instrument.
paras.zh: MIXS 首席研究员 (PI) 兼莱斯特大学空间研究所所长 Emma Bunce 教授对这一结果表示欢迎，认为这是负责开发该仪器的国际团队的一项重大成就。

paras.en: Professor Bunce said: "We have waited a long time to make measurements with MIXS and it is fantastic to see it operating brilliantly in space. This is testament to our engineering and technical team, and our international partners who we have worked with over many years to build this incredible instrument. 80% of the technology on MIXS is new!
paras.zh: Bunce教授表示：“我们已经等了很长时间才用MIXS进行测量，很高兴看到它在太空中出色地运行。这证明了我们的工程和技术团队以及我们多年来合作建造这台令人难以置信的仪器的国际合作伙伴。MIXS上80%的技术都是新技术！

paras.en: "During our calibration observations we have determined that MIXS is generally performing fantastically well in space! We have no effects in our images that are associated with 'stray light' (optical photons getting in when they should not). We continue to see effects of galactic cosmic rays as we did during cruise, but we understand these and can filter them out. We see some self-fluorescence which appears when the Sun is illuminating the optic, but this won't affect our dayside observations of Mercury's surface. And the detector has suffered no radiation damage after 8 years in space.
paras.zh: “在我们的校准观测过程中，我们确定 MIXS 在太空中通常表现得非常好！我们的图像中没有与‘杂散光’（光学光子在不应该进入的时候进入）相关的影响。我们继续看到银河宇宙射线的影响，就像我们在巡航期间所做的那样，但我们了解这些并可以将它们过滤掉。我们看到一些当太阳照亮光学器件时出现的自荧光，但这不会影响我们对水星的白天观测并且探测器在太空中运行8年也没有受到任何辐射损伤。

paras.en: "We see some effects in the instrument that we are still studying and expect to undertake some optimization procedures during the Mercury commissioning phase to fine tune MIXS in preparation for the science phase."
paras.zh: “我们看到了仍在研究的仪器中的一些影响，并期望在 Mercury 调试阶段进行一些优化程序，以微调 MIXS，为科学阶段做好准备。”

paras.en: The results suggest that the telescope has weathered its long exposure to the harsh space environment exceptionally well. Engineers have found no unwanted visible light interfering with its images, and the effects of high-energy cosmic rays are understood well enough to be removed during data processing.
paras.zh: 结果表明，该望远镜在长期暴露于恶劣的太空环境中表现得非常好。工程师们发现没有不需要的可见光干扰其图像，并且高能宇宙射线的影响已被充分理解，可以在数据处理过程中消除。

paras.en: The team has also identified a small amount of X-ray emission originating within the instrument itself when sunlight strikes its optics. However, this effect is not expected to interfere with observations of Mercury's sunlit surface. Most importantly, the detector shows no signs of radiation damage after eight years in space.
paras.zh: 该团队还发现，当阳光照射到仪器的光学器件时，仪器本身会发出少量 X 射线。然而，这种效应预计不会干扰对水星阳光照射表面的观测。最重要的是，探测器在太空中运行八年后没有显示出任何辐射损坏的迹象。

paras.en: Some remaining effects still require investigation, and scientists expect to make further adjustments after the spacecraft reaches Mercury to ensure that MIXS is ready for its full scientific mission.
paras.zh: 一些剩余的影响仍然需要调查，科学家们预计在航天器到达水星后进行进一步的调整，以确保 MIXS 为其完整的科学任务做好准备。

paras.en: How X-Rays Will Reveal Mercury's Hidden Chemistry
paras.zh: X 射线将如何揭示水星隐藏的化学成分

paras.en: BepiColombo is designed to investigate Mercury in unprecedented detail. As the smallest and one of the least explored rocky planets in our solar system, Mercury offers scientists a rare opportunity to understand how planets form and change under the extreme conditions found close to a star.
paras.zh: BepiColombo 旨在以前所未有的细节研究水星。作为太阳系中最小且探索最少的岩石行星之一，水星为科学家提供了一个难得的机会来了解行星在靠近恒星的极端条件下如何形成和变化。

paras.en: One of the mission's major goals is to uncover the planet's chemical composition and geological history. These findings could help explain Mercury's unusual characteristics while providing broader insights into the formation and evolution of the solar system.
paras.zh: 该任务的主要目标之一是揭示地球的化学成分和地质历史。这些发现可以帮助解释水星的不寻常特征，同时为太阳系的形成和演化提供更广泛的见解。

paras.en: MIXS, carried aboard the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO), will play a central role in this investigation. Developed by a European consortium led by the University of Leicester, it draws on the university's long history of X-ray astronomy research.
paras.zh: MIXS 搭载在水星行星轨道飞行器 (MPO) 上，将在这项调查中发挥核心作用。它由莱斯特大学领导的欧洲财团开发，借鉴了该大学悠久的 X 射线天文学研究历史。

paras.en: It is the first imaging X-ray telescope to operate on a planetary science mission. Working alongside other scientific instruments, MIXS will help produce a global map showing the elements that make up Mercury's surface, revealing its atomic composition in greater detail than ever before. It is also the only UK-led scientific instrument aboard BepiColombo and receives support from the UK Space Agency.
paras.zh: 它是第一台执行行星科学任务的成像 X 射线望远镜。与其他科学仪器一起工作，MIXS 将帮助制作一张全球地图，显示构成水星表面的元素，比以往更详细地揭示其原子组成。它也是 BepiColombo 上唯一由英国主导的科学仪器，并得到英国航天局的支持。

paras.en: The instrument works by detecting fluorescent X-rays released by rocks on Mercury's surface. When powerful X-rays from the Sun strike these rocks, they can cause atoms within the material to emit X-rays of their own. Different elements produce characteristic X-ray signals, allowing scientists to identify what the surface is made of without collecting physical samples.
paras.zh: 该仪器的工作原理是检测水星表面岩石释放的荧光 X 射线。当来自太阳的强大 X 射线撞击这些岩石时，它们会导致材料内的原子发射自己的 X 射线。不同的元素会产生特征性的 X 射线信号，使科学家能够在不收集物理样本的情况下识别表面的成分。

paras.en: MIXS will make these measurements with assistance from the Solar Intensity X-ray and particle Spectrometer (SIXS), which monitors the solar radiation and particles reaching Mercury.
paras.zh: MIXS 将在太阳强度 X 射线和粒子光谱仪 (SIXS) 的帮助下进行这些测量，该光谱仪监测到达水星的太阳辐射和粒子。

paras.en: The telescope will also examine X-rays emitted from Mercury's nighttime surface when charged particles associated with the planet's magnetic environment strike it. These measurements could reveal important connections between Mercury's surface and the surrounding space environment.
paras.zh: 该望远镜还将检查当与水星磁环境相关的带电粒子撞击水星夜间表面时发出的X射线。这些测量可以揭示水星表面与周围空间环境之间的重要联系。

paras.en: A 10 Billion Kilometer Journey With a Personal Legacy
paras.zh: 100亿公里的旅程与个人遗产

paras.en: For Dr. Adrian Martindale, MIXS Instrument Scientist at the University of Leicester's School of Physics and Astronomy, the successful observations represent the culmination of more than two decades of work.
paras.zh: 对于莱斯特大学物理与天文学院 MIXS 仪器科学家 Adrian Martindale 博士来说，这次成功的观测代表了二十多年工作的顶峰。

paras.en: Martindale joined the project in 2003 while still an undergraduate student and has been involved in nearly every aspect of the instrument's development.
paras.zh: Martindale 于 2003 年加入该项目，当时他还是一名本科生，几乎参与了该仪器开发的各个方面。

paras.en: Dr. Martindale said: "BepiColombo, and MIXS in particular, are like part of my family. I've been involved since I was an undergraduate and touched almost every part of the instrument before it was launched.
paras.zh: Martindale 博士表示：“BepiColombo，尤其是 MIXS，就像我家庭的一部分。我从本科生起就参与其中，在该仪器推出之前几乎接触过该仪器的每个部分。

paras.en: "This first data is mind-blowing to me. The last time we could see through this telescope it was in the basement under the School of Physics and Astronomy in Leicester, but after a rocket launch, eight years in space and 10 billion kilometers traveled it looks just the same. I can't wait to see the science data it produces when we get into orbit."
paras.zh: “第一个数据对我来说是令人兴奋的。上次我们通过这台望远镜看到它是在莱斯特物理与天文学学院的地下室里，但在火箭发射后，在太空中呆了八年，旅行了 100 亿公里，它看起来还是一样。我迫不及待地想看到当我们进入轨道时它产生的科学数据。”

paras.en: The milestone also carries special meaning for the team because MIXS represents the scientific legacy of Professor George Fraser. Fraser was the instrument's original Principal Investigator and the driving force behind its innovative optical design before his death in March 2014.
paras.zh: 这一里程碑对于团队来说也具有特殊意义，因为 MIXS 代表了 George Fraser 教授的科学遗产。 Fraser 在 2014 年 3 月去世之前是该仪器的最初首席研究员，也是其创新光学设计背后的推动力。

paras.en: Professor Bunce added: "We are thinking of George as we operate MIXS fully in space for the first time and know that he would be very, very proud of the team and delighted at our first light observations."
paras.zh: 邦斯教授补充道：“当我们第一次在太空中完全操作 MIXS 时，我们想到了乔治，并且知道他会为我们的团队感到非常非常自豪，并对我们的第一次光观测感到高兴。”

paras.en: BepiColombo Prepares for Its Final Arrival at Mercury
paras.zh: BepiColombo 为最终抵达水星做准备

paras.en: BepiColombo began its arrival phase on September 3, when the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) separated from the spacecraft assembly.
paras.zh: BepiColombo 于 9 月 3 日开始抵达阶段，当时水星转移舱 (MTM) 与航天器组件分离。

paras.en: The remaining connected spacecraft are scheduled to enter orbit around Mercury on November 21. The two science orbiters, MPO and Mio, are then expected to separate on December 9 to 10, allowing them to prepare for their respective scientific operations.
paras.zh: 其余连接的航天器计划于 11 月 21 日进入水星周围轨道。然后，两个科学轨道器 MPO 和 Mio 预计将于 12 月 9 日至 10 日分离，以便它们为各自的科学操作做好准备。

paras.en: The mission's primary science phase is scheduled to begin in April 2027. Once underway, BepiColombo will investigate Mercury's surface, internal structure, magnetic field, and surrounding environment, helping scientists piece together the history of a planet that remains surprisingly mysterious despite its proximity to the Sun.
paras.zh: 该任务的主要科学阶段计划于 2027 年 4 月开始。一旦开始，BepiColombo 将调查水星的表面、内部结构、磁场和周围环境，帮助科学家拼凑出这颗行星的历史，尽管它靠近太阳，但它仍然令人惊讶地神秘。

paras.en: For the MIXS team, the successful first observations of the Crab Nebula offer an early indication of what the instrument may accomplish when it finally turns its attention to Mercury.
paras.zh: 对于 MIXS 团队来说，对蟹状星云的首次成功观测为该仪器最终将注意力转向水星时可能实现的目标提供了早期迹象。

paras.en: MIXS was developed through a partnership involving research institutions and technology companies across Europe. Participating organizations include:
paras.zh: MIXS 是通过欧洲研究机构和技术公司的合作开发的。参与组织包括：

paras.en: - United Kingdom: University of Leicester, The Open University, RAL, and Magna Parva
paras.zh: - 英国：莱斯特大学、开放大学、RAL 和 Magna Parva

paras.en: - Finland: University of Helsinki, FMI, Patria, SSF, Oxford Instruments, and Beneq
paras.zh: - 芬兰：赫尔辛基大学、FMI、Patria、SSF、Oxford Instruments 和 Beneq

paras.en: - Germany: MPS, MPG-HLL, MPE, and PNSensor
paras.zh: - 德国：MPS、MPG-HLL、MPE 和 PNSensor

paras.en: UK funding for the BepiColombo MIXS instrument comes from the UK Space Agency, which serves as the lead funding organization, along with STFC, the European Space Agency, and the University of Leicester.
paras.zh: 英国对 BepiColombo MIXS 仪器的资助来自作为牵头资助组织的英国航天局，以及 STFC、欧洲航天局和莱斯特大学。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of Leicester. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由莱斯特大学提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 is now so far away that light takes 24 hours to reach it

paras.en: NASAâs Voyager 1 is now so far away that light takes 24 hours to reach it
paras.zh: NASA 的 Voyager 1 号距离我们如此遥远，光需要 24 小时才能到达

paras.en: - NASAâs Voyager 1 has reached an extraordinary milestone, traveling 16.1 billion miles from Earth to become the first spacecraft so distant that its signals take a full day to reach us. Nearly 50 years after launch, the aging probe continues its historic journey through interstellar space, pushing the limits of human exploration despite dwindling power and technical challenges.
paras.zh: - NASA 的航行者 1 号已经达到了一个非凡的里程碑，它距离地球 161 亿英里，成为第一艘距离如此遥远、其信号需要一整天才能到达我们的航天器。发射近 50 年后，这艘老化的探测器继续其穿越星际空间的历史性旅程，尽管动力和技术挑战日益减弱，但仍突破了人类探索的极限。

paras.en: NASA's Voyager 1 has achieved another extraordinary milestone, becoming the first spacecraft to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth. After more than 49 years of traveling through space, humanity's most distant spacecraft is now approximately 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers) from home. At that distance, even a signal moving at the speed of light needs an entire day to make the journey.
paras.zh: NASA 的航行者一号实现了另一个非凡的里程碑，成为第一艘到达距地球一光日距离的航天器。经过 49 年多的太空旅行，人类最远的航天器现在距离地球约 161 亿英里（259 亿公里）。在这个距离上，即使是以光速移动的信号也需要一整天的时间才能完成。

paras.en: The historic moment occurred on November 18 at 2:16 a.m. PST (5:16 a.m. EST). Scientists and engineers at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, which is managed by Caltech, received a signal from Voyager 1 early Thursday, exactly 24 hours after the spacecraft reached the milestone.
paras.zh: 这一历史性时刻发生在太平洋标准时间 11 月 18 日凌晨 2:16（美国东部标准时间凌晨 5:16）。美国宇航局位于南加州、由加州理工学院管理的喷气推进实验室 (JPL) 的科学家和工程师周四早些时候收到了航行者 1 号发出的信号，此时正好是航天器到达这一里程碑的 24 小时后。

paras.en: The achievement marks another remarkable chapter for a probe that has traveled farther than any other human-made object, survived decades beyond its original mission, and continues to explore a region of space that no spacecraft had previously entered.
paras.zh: 这一成就标志着探测器又开启了一个非凡的篇章，该探测器的飞行距离比任何其他人造物体都更远，在超出其最初任务数十年的情况下幸存下来，并继续探索以前没有航天器进入过的太空区域。

paras.en: Voyager 1 Is Now 24 Light-Hours From Earth
paras.zh: 航海者 1 号现在距地球 24 光小时

paras.en: Astronomers often describe enormous cosmic distances in terms of how long light takes to travel them. A light-day represents the distance light covers in 24 hours, or roughly 16.1 billion miles.
paras.zh: 天文学家经常用光传播所需的时间来描述巨大的宇宙距离。一个光日代表光在 24 小时内走过的距离，即大约 161 亿英里。

paras.en: Light moves through a vacuum at approximately 186,000 miles (299,000 kilometers) per second. To put Voyager 1's distance in perspective, sunlight passing Earth takes only about 1.3 seconds to reach the Moon. Reaching Neptune takes roughly four hours, while traveling from Neptune to Voyager 1 requires another 20 hours.
paras.zh: 光以每秒约 186,000 英里（299,000 公里）的速度穿过真空。从旅行者一号的距离来看，阳光穿过地球只需大约 1.3 秒即可到达月球。到达海王星大约需要 4 小时，而从海王星到航海者 1 号还需要 20 小时。

paras.en: Even these enormous distances are small compared with those separating stars. A single light-year, the distance light travels in one year, measures approximately 5.88 trillion miles (9.46 trillion kilometers).
paras.zh: 与那些分开的恒星相比，即使如此巨大的距离也很小。一光年，即光在一年内传播的距离，大约为 5.88 万亿英里（9.46 万亿公里）。

paras.en: Voyager 1's extraordinary distance also creates a major challenge for mission controllers. Sending a command to the spacecraft now requires 24 hours, and receiving a response takes another 24 hours. A complete exchange therefore spans two full days, even though the signals travel at the fastest speed possible.
paras.zh: 航行者一号非凡的距离也给任务控制人员带来了重大挑战。现在向航天器发送命令需要 24 小时，接收响应还需要 24 小时。因此，即使信号以尽可能最快的速度传输，一次完整的交换也需要整整两天。

paras.en: The milestone comes as engineers investigate a communication problem. NASA has not received scientific or engineering data from Voyager 1 since November 14. However, the probe continues transmitting a carrier signal, the radio signal that normally carries information back to Earth. By tracking this signal and calculating the spacecraft's trajectory, mission specialists were able to verify that Voyager 1 had crossed the one light-day mark. Engineers are continuing to investigate why the expected data is not coming through.
paras.zh: 这一里程碑是在工程师调查通信问题时出现的。自 11 月 14 日以来，NASA 尚未收到航行者 1 号的科学或工程数据。不过，探测器仍在继续发射载波信号，即通常将信息带回地球的无线电信号。通过跟踪该信号并计算航天器的轨迹，任务专家能够验证旅行者一号已经跨越了一光日标记。工程师们正在继续调查为什么预期数据没有得到。

paras.en: A Historic Journey Beyond the Solar System's Planets
paras.zh: 超越太阳系行星的历史性旅程

paras.en: Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, were launched in 1977 to take advantage of an unusual arrangement of the outer planets. The alignment allowed the spacecraft to use planetary gravity to travel from one destination to another, making an ambitious exploration mission possible.
paras.zh: 航海者 1 号及其双胞胎航海者 2 号于 1977 年发射，旨在利用外行星的不寻常排列。这种对准使得航天器能够利用行星重力从一个目的地旅行到另一个目的地，从而使一项雄心勃勃的探索任务成为可能。

paras.en: Managed by JPL, the Voyagers became the third and fourth spacecraft to visit Jupiter and Saturn. They also delivered the first high-resolution images of these distant planets, revealing extraordinary new details about their atmospheres, rings, and moons. Voyager 2 continued farther, becoming the first spacecraft to explore Uranus and Neptune up close.
paras.zh: 在喷气推进实验室的管理下，航海者号成为第三和第四艘访问木星和土星的航天器。他们还提供了这些遥远行星的第一批高分辨率图像，揭示了有关它们的大气层、环和卫星的非凡新细节。航海家二号继续走得更远，成为第一艘近距离探索天王星和海王星的航天器。

paras.en: Today, both probes are traveling through interstellar space, making them humanity's only spacecraft to have crossed into the region beyond the Sun's protective bubble. Their instruments continue monitoring changes in the Sun's magnetic field across immense distances, providing scientists with measurements that cannot be collected from Earth.
paras.zh: 如今，这两个探测器正在穿越星际空间，成为人类唯一进入太阳保护罩之外区域的航天器。他们的仪器持续监测远距离太阳磁场的变化，为科学家提供无法从地球收集的测量结果。

paras.en: "Traveling a light-day is a singular feat for a spacecraft, but Voyager is so much more than a distant traveler. The Voyager mission would be remarkable just for what it contributed to planetary science with the Grand Tour of the outer planets," said Joe Westlake, director, Heliophysics Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. "But it went on to become central to NASA's fleet of heliophysics missions offering insights into the star that we all revolve around, the Sun."
paras.zh: “航行一光日对于航天器来说是一项非凡的壮举，但航行者号不仅仅是一个遥远的旅行者。航行者号任务将是非凡的，因为它通过外行星大巡游为行星科学做出了贡献，”美国宇航局华盛顿总部太阳物理学部主任乔·韦斯特莱克说。 “但它后来成为美国宇航局太阳物理学任务的核心，为我们提供对我们围绕的恒星——太阳的深入了解。”

paras.en: "Voyager 1 crossing the light-day threshold is yet another historic feat on an extraordinary voyage of discovery," said Dave Gallagher, JPL director. "Above all, this milestone stands as a testament to the exceptional teams who built, programmed, and fly these spacecraft today, and who have overcome countless challenges to keep them connected to Earth across the vastness of space. As NASA pushes toward new frontiers in human and robotic exploration, Voyager and the people behind its success continue to inspire us to reach farther and dream bigger."
paras.zh: 喷气推进实验室主任戴夫·加拉格尔 (Dave Gallagher) 表示：“航海家一号跨越光日门槛是非凡发现之旅中的又一历史性壮举。” “最重要的是，这一里程碑证明了今天建造、编程和驾驶这些航天器的杰出团队，他们克服了无数的挑战，使它们在浩瀚的太空中保持与地球的联系。随着美国宇航局 (NASA) 向人类和机器人探索的新领域推进，航海者号及其成功背后的人们继续激励我们走得更远，梦想更大。”

paras.en: Voyager's Golden Record Carries a Message From Earth
paras.zh: 航行者号的金唱片承载着来自地球的信息

paras.en: The Voyager spacecraft carry more than scientific instruments. Each also holds a Golden Record, a gold-plated copper phonograph record containing images and sounds representing life on Earth. These recordings were designed as messages that an advanced extraterrestrial civilization might discover someday.
paras.zh: 航行者号宇宙飞船携带的不仅仅是科学仪器。每个人还持有一张金唱片，这是一张镀金铜留声机唱片，其中包含代表地球生命的图像和声音。这些录音被设计为先进的外星文明有一天可能会发现的信息。

paras.en: The records give the mission a purpose extending far beyond its scientific discoveries. Even after the spacecraft eventually lose the ability to communicate with Earth, they will continue traveling through space with a small collection of sights and sounds from the planet that launched them.
paras.zh: 这些记录赋予这次任务的目的远远超出了其科学发现。即使航天器最终失去了与地球通信的能力，它们仍将继续在太空中旅行，并带着来自发射它们的行星的少量景象和声音。

paras.en: "Nearly half a century after leaving Earth, the Voyager mission continues to push the boundaries of human exploration. Its epic journey reflects the vision of Ed Stone, the Caltech physicist and JPL director who guided the mission for decades, and the curiosity and tenacity of generations of scientists and engineers who have carried that vision forward," said Ray Jayawardhana, president, Caltech. "Beyond its immense contributions to science, Voyager also captures something profound about the human spirit. We may never know where its journey will ultimately lead, but it will venture on, an enduring affirmation that humanity was here and we yearned to explore."
paras.zh: 加州理工学院校长雷·贾亚瓦德哈纳 (Ray Jayawardhana) 表示：“离开地球近半个世纪后，旅行者号任务继续突破人类探索的界限。其史诗般的旅程反映了数十年来指导该任务的加州理工学院物理学家兼喷气推进实验室主任埃德·斯通 (Ed Stone) 的愿景，以及推动这一愿景的几代科学家和工程师的好奇心和坚韧。” “除了对科学的巨大贡献之外，航海者号还捕捉到了人类精神的一些深刻的东西。我们可能永远不知道它的旅程最终将通向何方，但它会继续冒险，持久地证明人类就在这里，我们渴望探索。”

paras.en: Exploring the Mysterious Region Beyond the Sun
paras.zh: 探索太阳之外的神秘区域

paras.en: Voyager 1 is currently moving through space at approximately 38,000 mph (61,155 kph). In 2012, it became the first spacecraft to cross the boundary of the heliosphere, a vast region surrounding the Sun that is filled with particles and magnetic fields generated by our star.
paras.zh: 旅行者 1 号目前正以大约 38,000 英里/小时（61,155 公里/小时）的速度在太空中移动。 2012年，它成为第一个跨越日光层边界的航天器，日光层是太阳周围的广阔区域，充满了恒星产生的粒子和磁场。

paras.en: This protective bubble helps shield the solar system from cosmic radiation arriving from elsewhere in the galaxy. Beyond its outer boundary lies interstellar space, where particles and magnetic fields from the broader galaxy become more dominant.
paras.zh: 这个保护性气泡有助于保护太阳系免受来自银河系其他地方的宇宙辐射的影响。在其外边界之外是星际空间，来自更广阔星系的粒子和磁场在其中变得更加占主导地位。

paras.en: Voyager 2 followed a different route and crossed into interstellar space in 2018. Together, the probes are providing the first direct observations of conditions beyond the heliosphere.
paras.zh: 航行者 2 号沿着不同的路线于 2018 年进入星际空间。这些探测器共同首次对日光层以外的情况进行直接观测。

paras.en: One of their most intriguing discoveries is that the Sun's effects do not simply disappear at the boundary. Its influence appears to extend much farther into interstellar space than scientists once understood, raising new questions about where the environment shaped by our star truly gives way to the surrounding galaxy.
paras.zh: 他们最有趣的发现之一是太阳的影响不会简单地在边界处消失。它的影响力似乎比科学家们曾经理解的更远地延伸到了星际空间，这引发了新的问题：我们的恒星塑造的环境在哪里真正让位于周围的星系。

paras.en: "The Voyagers are revolutionizing our understanding of interstellar space, a previously unexplored region outside the heliosphere," said Linda Spilker, Voyager project scientist at JPL. "One big surprise is the extent to which our Sun continues to affect interstellar space, all the way out to Voyager 1. Where does the Sun's influence end and pristine interstellar space begin? Perhaps Voyager may endure long enough to answer that question."
paras.zh: 喷气推进实验室航海者号项目科学家琳达·斯皮尔克 (Linda Spilker) 表示：“航海者号正在彻底改变我们对星际空间的理解，星际空间是日光层之外以前未经探索的区域。” “一个大惊喜是我们的太阳对星际空间的影响程度，一直到航海者一号。太阳的影响在哪里结束，原始星际空间从哪里开始？也许航海者号可以坚持足够长的时间来回答这个问题。”

paras.en: How NASA Is Keeping Voyager 1 Alive After Nearly 50 Years
paras.zh: NASA 如何在近 50 年后让航海者 1 号保持活力

paras.en: Operating spacecraft built nearly half a century ago requires increasingly inventive engineering. Both Voyagers have experienced problems as their equipment ages, including clogged thrusters and a malfunctioning computer. NASA engineers have repeatedly developed solutions that allow the probes to continue working despite these setbacks.
paras.zh: 运行近半个世纪前建造的航天器需要越来越有创意的工程。随着设备老化，两艘航海者号都遇到了问题，包括推进器堵塞和计算机故障。美国宇航局工程师反复开发解决方案，使探测器能够在遇到这些挫折的情况下继续工作。

paras.en: Electricity has become one of the mission's greatest limitations. Earlier in 2026, engineers took a calculated risk by switching off three devices aboard Voyager 1 and replacing them with three alternatives that consume less power. This change was intended to help the spacecraft stretch its remaining energy supply.
paras.zh: 电力已成为任务的最大限制之一。 2026 年初，工程师们冒着计算过的风险，关闭了 Voyager 1 号上的三台设备，并用三种功耗更低的替代品替换它们。这一变化旨在帮助航天器延长其剩余的能源供应。

paras.en: Voyager 1 depends on a radioisotope thermal generator that is now approximately 50 years old. Often described as a nuclear battery, the device produces electricity by converting heat released during the radioactive decay of plutonium.
paras.zh: 航行者 1 号依赖于放射性同位素热发电机，该发电机已有大约 50 年的历史。该装置通常被描述为核电池，通过转化钚放射性衰变过程中释放的热量来发电。

paras.en: As the radioactive material continues to decay, the available power gradually decreases. Both Voyager spacecraft lose approximately four watts of electrical output every year, forcing engineers to make difficult decisions about which systems can remain operational.
paras.zh: 随着放射性物质继续衰变，可用功率逐渐减少。两艘航行者号航天器每年都会损失大约四瓦的电力输出，迫使工程师就哪些系统可以保持运行做出艰难的决定。

paras.en: The latest conservation measures are expected to provide enough power to operate the spacecraft's current scientific instruments until at least the summer of 2027, when both probes will celebrate their 50th launch anniversaries.
paras.zh: 最新的保护措施预计将至少在 2027 年夏天之前提供足够的电力来操作航天器当前的科学仪器，届时两个探测器将庆祝其发射 50 周年。

paras.en: One Day, Voyager 1 Will Become a Silent Messenger to the Stars
paras.zh: 总有一天，航海家一号将成为一位无声的星空信使

paras.en: Maintaining contact across such staggering distances requires some of NASA's most powerful communications equipment. The agency relies on its Deep Space Network, a worldwide system of large radio antennas located at three facilities, to communicate with Voyager and other spacecraft traveling to and beyond the Moon.
paras.zh: 在如此惊人的距离内保持联系需要美国宇航局最强大的通信设备。该机构依靠其深空网络（一个由位于三个设施的大型无线电天线组成的全球系统）与航行者号和其他往返月球的航天器进行通信。

paras.en: Despite the enormous communication delay and the spacecraft's aging systems, engineers continue monitoring Voyager 1 daily and transmitting instructions every week. The mission remains an extraordinary demonstration of what long-term spacecraft engineering can achieve.
paras.zh: 尽管存在巨大的通信延迟和航天器系统的老化，工程师们仍继续每天监控航行者一号并每周传输指令。这次任务仍然是长期航天器工程可以实现的目标的非凡展示。

paras.en: "We listen to Voyager 1 every day and send commands to the spacecraft weekly. It just takes a little longer to communicate than it used to," said Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager at JPL. "Even traveling at the speed of light, signals now take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft and 24 hours to reach us. One day in the future, when it can no longer communicate with Earth, Voyager 1 will become humanity's silent ambassador to the stars."
paras.zh: “我们每天收听航行者一号，每周向航天器发送命令。只是沟通时间比以前长一点，”喷气推进实验室航海者号项目经理苏珊娜·多德 (Suzanne Dodd) 说。 “即使以光速行进，信号现在也需要24小时才能到达航天器，24小时才能到达我们。在未来的某一天，当它不再能与地球通讯时，航海家一号将成为人类无声的星际大使。”

articles.title: Microplastics may be more dangerous than we thought. Scientists just discovered why

paras.en: Microplastics may be more dangerous than we thought. Scientists just discovered why
paras.zh: 微塑料可能比我们想象的更危险。科学家刚刚发现原因

paras.en: - Microplastics may be doing something far more dangerous than simply accumulating in our bodies. Scientists have discovered that tiny plastic particles can interact with water to generate highly reactive molecules capable of damaging cells and tissues. This unexpected chemical activity could help explain growing evidence linking microplastic exposure to serious health problems, including heart attacks, strokes, and neurological disorders.
paras.zh: - 微塑料可能会做一些比简单地在我们体内积累更危险的事情。科学家发现，微小的塑料颗粒可以与水相互作用，产生能够破坏细胞和组织的高反应性分子。这种意想不到的化学活性可能有助于解释越来越多的证据表明接触微塑料与严重的健康问题有关，包括心脏病、中风和神经系统疾病。

paras.en: Plastic is used in everything from food packaging and water bottles to children's toys, largely because it is considered chemically stable and unlikely to react with its surroundings. However, new research suggests that this assumption may not hold when plastic breaks down into extremely small particles.
paras.zh: 塑料被用于从食品包装、水瓶到儿童玩具的各种产品中，主要是因为它被认为化学性质稳定，不太可能与周围环境发生反应。然而，新的研究表明，当塑料分解成极小的颗粒时，这种假设可能不成立。

paras.en: As larger plastic objects fragment into microplastics and even smaller nanoplastics, the amount of exposed surface area increases dramatically. Scientists have now discovered that these newly exposed surfaces can interact with water in unexpected ways, producing reactive molecules that may harm living cells.
paras.zh: 随着较大的塑料物体碎裂成微塑料甚至更小的纳米塑料，暴露的表面积急剧增加。科学家们现在发现，这些新暴露的表面可以以意想不到的方式与水相互作用，产生可能损害活细胞的反应分子。

paras.en: Researchers at Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley identified the chemical processes behind this phenomenon in a new study published in Nature. Their findings challenge the longstanding idea that microplastics are simply passive fragments of material.
paras.zh: 哥伦比亚大学和加州大学伯克利分校的研究人员在《自然》杂志上发表的一项新研究中确定了这一现象背后的化学过程。他们的发现挑战了长期以来的观点，即微塑料只是材料的被动碎片。

paras.en: "As plastic fragments into smaller and smaller particles, its surface area increases enormously. Then microplastics change the water that surrounds them, generating high-energy, reactive radicals (reactive oxygen species, ROS) that very likely contribute to biological damage that we see in animals and potentially in humans as a result of microplastic exposure," said Wei Min, a Columbia professor of Chemistry and Biomedical Engineering.
paras.zh: “随着塑料碎片分解成越来越小的颗粒，其表面积极大地增加。然后微塑料改变了它们周围的水，产生高能活性自由基（活性氧，ROS），这很可能导致我们在动物和人类中看到的由于微塑料暴露而造成的生物损伤，”哥伦比亚大学化学与生物医学工程教授魏敏说。

paras.en: Why Microplastics Could Be Dangerous Inside the Human Body
paras.zh: 为什么微塑料在人体内可能是危险的

paras.en: The discovery raises important questions about what happens when microplastics enter the human body. Blood and cells contain large amounts of water, creating conditions in which these tiny particles could continue participating in chemical reactions.
paras.zh: 这一发现提出了有关微塑料进入人体后会发生什么的重要问题。血液和细胞含有大量的水，为这些微小颗粒可以继续参与化学反应创造了条件。

paras.en: Rather than remaining inactive after exposure, microplastics may generate reactive oxygen species, often called ROS. These highly reactive molecules can damage biological structures, including components of cells and tissues. The findings offer a possible explanation for some of the harmful effects associated with microplastic exposure, although they do not establish that this process causes specific diseases in humans.
paras.zh: 微塑料在暴露后不会保持不活跃状态，而是可能会产生活性氧，通常称为活性氧。这些高反应性分子会损害生物结构，包括细胞和组织的成分。这些发现为与微塑料暴露相关的一些有害影响提供了可能的解释，尽管他们并没有确定这一过程会导致人类的特定疾病。

paras.en: The research builds on earlier work by Min's laboratory that helped reveal just how widespread microscopic plastic contamination has become.
paras.zh: 这项研究建立在敏实验室早期工作的基础上，该工作有助于揭示微观塑料污染的普遍程度。

paras.en: In a widely reported 2024 study, the Columbia researchers developed a laser-based microscopy technique capable of detecting extremely small plastic particles. Using this technology, they found an average of approximately 240,000 detectable plastic fragments in a single liter of bottled water (mostly nanometer-sized plastic, nanoplastics). That was 10 to 100 times more particles than previous estimates had suggested.
paras.zh: 在一项广泛报道的 2024 年研究中，哥伦比亚研究人员开发了一种基于激光的显微镜技术，能够检测极小的塑料颗粒。利用这项技术，他们在一升瓶装水中平均发现了大约24万个可检测的塑料碎片（大部分是纳米尺寸的塑料、纳米塑料）。这比之前估计的颗粒物数量多出 10 到 100 倍。

paras.en: The discovery helped draw greater attention to the presence of microplastics and nanoplastics throughout the food system.
paras.zh: 这一发现有助于引起人们对整个食品系统中微塑料和纳米塑料的更多关注。

paras.en: Growing Concerns About Microplastics and Human Health
paras.zh: 人们对微塑料和人类健康的担忧日益加深

paras.en: Since that earlier research attracted widespread attention, the potential health consequences of microplastic exposure have become an increasingly important public health issue.
paras.zh: 由于早期的研究引起了广泛关注，微塑料暴露的潜在健康后果已成为一个日益重要的公共卫生问题。

paras.en: In 2026, the federal government launched a $144 million initiative focused on addressing toxic microplastics in the human body. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency also added microplastics to a federal list of contaminants that may be of concern in drinking water, marking their first appearance on the list.
paras.zh: 2026 年，联邦政府启动了一项耗资 1.44 亿美元的计划，重点解决人体内的有毒微塑料问题。美国环境保护署还将微塑料添加到饮用水中可能引起关注的联邦污染物清单中，这是它们首次出现在该清单中。

paras.en: Meanwhile, studies published in major scientific journals, including the New England Journal of Medicine, Nature Medicine, and Nature Health, have reported associations between exposure to microplastics and nanoplastics and serious conditions such as heart attacks, strokes, dementia, and brain tumors.
paras.zh: 与此同时，《新英格兰医学杂志》、《自然医学》和《自然健康》等主要科学期刊上发表的研究报告称，接触微塑料和纳米塑料与心脏病、中风、痴呆和脑肿瘤等严重疾病之间存在关联。

paras.en: However, an important question has remained unanswered. If plastic is generally considered chemically inert, how might these microscopic fragments contribute to biological damage?
paras.zh: 然而，一个重要的问题仍未得到解答。如果塑料通常被认为具有化学惰性，那么这些微小碎片如何导致生物损伤？

paras.en: The new findings identify a previously overlooked chemical pathway that could help researchers understand these potential health risks.
paras.zh: 新发现发现了一个以前被忽视的化学途径，可以帮助研究人员了解这些潜在的健康风险。

paras.en: "Our research found that when microplastics interact with water, as they do when they're in bottled water, or when they're absorbed into our bloodstream, they spontaneously generate what we call reactive oxygen species (ROS)," said Naixin Qian, a postdoctoral researcher in Wei Min's lab who helped lead the research. "ROS are textbook examples of the kinds of molecules that can damage animal and human tissue."
paras.zh: “我们的研究发现，当微塑料与水相互作用时，就像它们在瓶装水中一样，或者当它们被吸收到我们的血液中时，它们会自发地产生我们所说的活性氧（ROS），”帮助领导这项研究的魏民实验室博士后研究员钱乃新说。 “ROS 是可以损害动物和人体组织的分子类型的教科书示例。”

paras.en: How Water Triggers Harmful Chemical Reactions
paras.zh: 水如何引发有害的化学反应

paras.en: One of the most surprising aspects of the discovery is that water plays an active role in the reaction.
paras.zh: 这一发现最令人惊讶的方面之一是水在反应中发挥着积极的作用。

paras.en: Many plastics are hydrophobic, meaning their surfaces repel water. When water encounters these surfaces, the molecules and electrically charged particles near the boundary can behave differently than they do in ordinary water.
paras.zh: 许多塑料都是疏水性的，这意味着它们的表面防水。当水遇到这些表面时，边界附近的分子和带电粒子的行为可能与普通水中不同。
